points_of_interest.description: Beneath the sun carpet lies the entrance to the castle's temporal control systems. The FLOOR of the welcome hall is the ceiling of the time machine. Every dignitary who ever walked across that carpet was standing on top of reality-manipulation equipment.

points_of_interest.name: The Aquarium Tunnel
points_of_interest.description: The aquarium room contains a hole in the wall leading to Fish Tank on one side, and on the other side, a tunnel that drops into Vanilla Basement (Maze). The aquarium is not just decorative—it's a concealed access point between the main floor and the basement labyrinth.

subsections.name: The Beta Lobby Network — Five Echoes
subsections.description:
Five Beta Lobbies (A through E) exist as simplified versions of the castle lobby, their structure and textures frozen in the state of the castle as it appeared during the Shoshinkai 1995 demonstration. Waluigi must emphasize: these are not historical reconstructions. They are PRESERVED TEMPORAL STATES. The castle as it existed in 1995 is still accessible, still functional, and still connected to the rest of the castle network.

Each Beta Lobby contains numbered painting rooms leading to 'beta' versions of the painting worlds—Mountain, Snow Slider, Fire Bubble, Water Land. These are the ORIGINAL versions of these locations, before they were refined into their current states. The beta worlds still exist. They were never destroyed. They were simply... left behind, like rooms in a house that no one visits anymore but that still have the lights on.

The Beta Lobbies are connected to each other through a hierarchy. Looking at the ceiling with sufficient Power Stars warps between lobbies. Trap doors connect others. Beta Lobby D connects to the main Basement and Beta Basement. Beta Lobby C connects to the 4th Floor and Crimson Hallway. The network forms a PARALLEL INFRASTRUCTURE through the castle—an older version of the transit system that still functions alongside the current one.

points_of_interest.name: The Ceiling Warps
points_of_interest.description: Looking at the ceiling with 10+ Power Stars triggers inter-lobby warps. The ceiling is a PORTAL. The castle's original architects embedded dimensional transit into the act of LOOKING UP. Waluigi wonders how many people have accidentally teleported by staring at the ceiling.

points_of_interest.name: The Kuppa1 Trap Doors
points_of_interest.description: Before collecting any red Power Stars, trap doors in Beta Lobbies A, C, and E lead to 'Kuppa1'—what appears to be a prototype of the Bowser battles. The name 'Kuppa' is the Japanese name for Bowser. This suggests the Beta Lobbies preserve not just the castle's architecture but its THREATS. The original Bowser encounter is still accessible.

points_of_interest.name: Beta Lobby E — The Deadly Grounds Entrance
points_of_interest.description: Beta Lobby E is specifically accessed from 'Deadly Grounds'—a corrupted, lethal version of the Castle Grounds. The fact that the most dangerous entrance leads to the most primitive lobby version suggests a temporal relationship: the more corrupted the approach, the older the castle state you access.

subsections.name: Crescent Castle — The Shadow Twin
subsections.description:
Crescent Castle is an alternate version of the castle's interior, accessed by entering the castle's BACK DOORS from the Vanilla Castle Grounds. While the main castle is entered through the front, the shadow castle is entered from behind. The symbolism is not subtle.

The main floor consists of a large lobby with hallways beneath a crescent moon, painting rooms, and connections to the basement through a warp pipe. But several features distinguish it from its 'normal' counterpart. A hidden door in a sky-textured wall leads to Fake Lobby. A painting of Peach in a red-carpeted hallway warps to 'Delicious Cake'—and Waluigi STILL does not understand the cake dimension. A sky-textured hole in the floor leads to Castle Grounds—or, with a small random chance, to INVERTED Castle Grounds, where everything is upside down.

The randomness of the Inverted Castle Grounds warp is particularly alarming. You step on the same spot and USUALLY go to normal Castle Grounds, but SOMETIMES you end up in an inverted reality. The castle is ROLLING DICE with your destination. Waluigi does not appreciate gambling with dimensional physics.

points_of_interest.name: The Slide Room Variant
points_of_interest.description: A pipe drops visitors into an altered copy of the vanilla castle slide room, then a door leads to Dark Lobby. The slide has been REPURPOSED—it no longer serves as recreation but as a transit mechanism between dimensional states.

points_of_interest.name: The Peach Painting Warp
points_of_interest.description: Entering a painting of Peach in a red-carpeted hallway leads to 'Delicious Cake.' This warp is hidden in a hallway that also connects to Fake Lobby and the basement. It is remarkably easy to stumble into a cake dimension while trying to navigate to the basement.

points_of_interest.name: The Probability Floor
points_of_interest.description: A sky-textured hole usually leads to Castle Grounds but has a small random chance of sending you to Inverted Castle Grounds. The floor itself is making probabilistic decisions about your destination. The castle is not a building—it is a decision-making entity.

subsections.name: Parallel Lobby — The Alternative Architecture
subsections.description:
Parallel Lobby is the most complex main-floor area in the entire castle complex. It 'parallels' the vanilla castle structure with a first-floor lobby, circular second floor, and third floor leading to Bowser battles—but everything is LARGER, more convoluted, and riddled with hidden connections.

The first floor has orange sky murals instead of blue. Orange again—the same twilight-state color found in Floor 3B. The second floor is a circular room with U-shaped walls containing an absurd density of warps, painting rooms, mirror rooms, basement slides, and connections to at least a dozen other areas. A sun monument in the courtyard marks a slide to Basement Maze. A mirror room requires the Vanish Cap to access, contains a painting to No Man's Land, and leads through a blank white void room to Inverted Castle Grounds.

The third floor connects to Bowser's Domain, Nebula Lobby, and generates warp holes to Bowser's Airship and Kuppa1. The concentration of Bowser-related destinations on the third floor suggests this is the castle's MILITARY COMMAND level—the floor from which wars were coordinated and Bowser battles were staged.

Waluigi counts the connections from Parallel Lobby's second floor alone: Floor 3B, Floor 4B, Greenhouse Framework, Warped Internal Garden, Basement Maze, Castle Grounds, The City, No Man's Land, Inverted Castle Grounds, Hazy Memory Cave, Frosty Flowering Peak, Steep Green Summit, firebubble3, and Vanilla Lobby. FOURTEEN destinations from a single floor. This is not a lobby. This is a SWITCHBOARD.

points_of_interest.name: The Mirror Room
points_of_interest.description: Requires the Vanish Cap. Contains a painting to No Man's Land and a door through the mirror to a blank white void room. The lower door in the void leads to Inverted Castle Grounds. The upper door is UNREACHABLE by normal means—using cheats to enter it kills the player. A door that exists but CANNOT BE USED, and attempting to use it is LETHAL. What is behind that door?

points_of_interest.name: The Sun Monument Slide
points_of_interest.description: A sun monument in the courtyard marks a slide to a basement pipe leading to Basement Maze. Sun symbolism appears throughout the castle's transit systems. Solar Tower, sun carpets, sun monuments—the castle's architects associated the SUN with travel, transition, and access.

points_of_interest.name: The Third Floor Junction
points_of_interest.description: Three slopes lead to three rooms, each with a warp hole and double doors. The LEFT doors warp you to the RIGHT doors—spatial transposition disguised as architecture. The warp holes lead to Kuppa1, Bowser's Airship, Treetop Ride, and Wing Mario over the Floating Islands. Four destinations from three rooms, with spatial tricks making the room layout itself unreliable.

subsections.name: Nebula Lobby — The Celestial Hub
subsections.description:
A five-floor celestial-themed lobby that serves as one of the castle's major transit hubs. Waluigi considers Nebula Lobby one of the most strategically significant locations in the entire castle because of its VERTICAL REACH—five floors spanning from underground tunnels to a room directly below Bowser's Castle.

The second floor contains a sun carpet that warps to Stellar Tower (with sufficient stars). The third floor has a warp pipe to the 4th Floor, a clock face leading to Tick Tock Slide, and—behind a door marked with a prohibition sign—access to Bowser's Domain. A PROHIBITION SIGN on the door to Bowser's territory. Someone put up a 'no entry' sign. Waluigi appreciates the gesture but doubts its effectiveness.

The fourth floor has a bricked-over doorway—sealed deliberately. Whatever was behind that door was removed from the transit network. The fifth floor culminates in a hallway where a green Power Star can only be obtained with the Vanish Cap and 120 stars. This is the castle's MOST RESTRICTED reward, requiring both maximum power accumulation and dimensional manipulation to access.

The underwater tunnel connecting the third floor to the side area is particularly devious. Taking the RIGHT fork leads to the Flooded Basement—the permanent death trap with no escape. The tunnel looks identical in both directions. One path leads to valuable destinations. The other leads to eternal imprisonment. Choose wrong and you're gone.

points_of_interest.name: The Five-Floor Ascent
points_of_interest.description: First floor: entry corridor. Second floor: paintings to cloud and bullet dimensions, warp holes to snow and sky realms. Third floor: clock, Bowser access, underwater tunnel. Fourth floor: sealed door, three painting rooms. Fifth floor: maximum-security Power Star and Bowser's Castle entrance. Each floor increases in danger and significance.

points_of_interest.name: The Flooded Basement Fork
points_of_interest.description: The underwater tunnel's right fork leads to permanent entrapment. This is either a security measure to catch unauthorized swimmers or a deliberate disposal system. Swim right and you cease to exist in the normal castle.

points_of_interest.name: The Prohibition Door
points_of_interest.description: A door marked with a 🚫 sign leads to Bowser's Domain. Someone—possibly a frustrated Toad—put up a 'do not enter' sign on the door to the most dangerous location accessible from this lobby. Waluigi respects the energy but questions the strategy.

subsections.name: Corrupted & Anomalous Lobbies
subsections.description: Several lobby variants exist in states of dimensional corruption, temporal distortion, or fundamental wrongness. These are not damaged versions of normal lobbies—they are lobbies that have been ALTERED by forces that the castle's original architects may not have anticipated.

points_of_interest.name: Dark Lobby
points_of_interest.description: Dark brick walls, most doors non-functional, Boos in the upstairs hallway. The sun carpet ground-pound leads to EITHER Challenge Lobby or its corrupted variant—random chance determining whether you enter a functional space or a broken one. The castle is gambling with your safety.

points_of_interest.name: Fabricated Lobby & Corrupted Variant
points_of_interest.description: The Fabricated Lobby contains 'fabricated' reproductions of beta levels—copies of copies, replicas of prototypes. Its corrupted variant is darker, with a backwards-running clock, walled-over exits, and a Bowser portrait at the end of a dark hallway. Standing before the portrait warps you to an invisible platform above the lobby where a Power Star spawns. The castle REWARDS you for confronting the image of its conqueror. Why?

points_of_interest.name: Challenge Lobby (Corrupted)
points_of_interest.description: Silent except for a backwards-ticking clock. All doors walled up. The faceless Peach painting is MISSING. In the normal Challenge Lobby, Peach's faceless portrait is disturbing but present. In the corrupted version, even the disturbing image has been removed. Whatever the faceless portrait represented, the corruption has consumed it.

points_of_interest.name: Fake Lobby
points_of_interest.description: A shadow-shrouded version of the Vanilla Lobby where most doors are non-functional dummies. Based on prerelease beta footage—this is what the castle WOULD have looked like if development had gone differently. Ground-pounding the sun carpet leads to 'Mario's Maze.' The castle preserves alternate developmental paths as accessible realities.

points_of_interest.name: Monochrome Lobby
points_of_interest.description: The castle with all color removed. Empty painting rooms. A non-functional downstairs hallway. The upstairs leads to a circular room based on the mythical fourth floor and a warp pipe to 'World of Dreams.' Accessible only from the Monochrome Castle Grounds and only AFTER the main game—this is a POST-GAME area, suggesting the castle has states that only unlock after sufficient exploration. The castle reveals itself PROGRESSIVELY.

points_of_interest.name: Inverted Lobby
points_of_interest.description: Brown stone walls, inverted carpet and railing colors. Only two functional doors, both leading to hallways rather than the expected courtyard and basement. The Peach stained glass window hides a narrow opening to an empty room—visible but unreachable. The castle shows you what's hidden but prevents access. A TEASE built into the architecture.

points_of_interest.name: Dream Castle
points_of_interest.description: A basement-like area with a staircase, knocked-off doors, a Bowser portrait, and a solid black painting. A well shows a red Power Star in a flooded room below, blocked by a grate. The star can be reached via Metal and Vanish Caps through the well, or by manipulating water level pillars. The castle presents a PUZZLE—you can see the reward but must understand the building's mechanisms to claim it. The castle is TESTING its visitors.

subsections.name: Specialized Lobbies
subsections.description: Several lobby areas serve specific functions within the castle's network, each contributing unique capabilities to the overall system.

points_of_interest.name: Aventura Lobby
points_of_interest.description:
Five rooms with identical layout but different textures and coin colors—vanilla, beta, starry, inverted, and basement. Based on the 'Casa de Mario' attraction at Reino Aventura amusement park in Mexico City. The castle contains a REPLICA of a real-world attraction that was itself a replica of the castle. A copy of a copy. Reality referencing fiction referencing reality. Waluigi's head hurts.

The inverted room connects to the basement room through a hole in the wall. The basement room connects to the beta room through another hole. The rooms are not just connected by doors—they're PHYSICALLY BREAKING INTO EACH OTHER. The boundaries between dimensional states are dissolving.

points_of_interest.name: Mourning Star Lobby
points_of_interest.description: Characterized by sad blue stars and beta-themed walls. The name itself is a pun—'mourning' star, not 'morning.' This lobby is in GRIEF. It connects to Basement Annex, Basement Sewer, Bob-omb's Hideout, Toad's Lobby, and Aventura Lobby, making it a central junction for the lower castle network. A white-eyed Princess Peach painting warps to the Vanilla Lobby. White eyes—sightless, dead. The castle's representation of Peach in this grieving lobby has no life in her eyes.

points_of_interest.name: Genesis Lobby
points_of_interest.description: The name means 'beginning' or 'origin.' Accessible from the Castle Grounds through an underwater pool, this lobby connects to Beta Basement, Castle Depths, Floor 4B, Toad's Lobby, and contains a hedge maze with a Toad statue and warp pipe to Yellow Switch Palace. A GENESIS point connected to the castle's deepest levels and oldest states. This may be where the castle BEGAN—the original entrance before all the other lobbies were constructed.

points_of_interest.name: Nocturnal Lobby
points_of_interest.description: Royal blue starry walls with Peach and Bowser portraits. Contains a miniature version of Peach's castle inside an aquarium—jumping into it warps to Vanilla Castle Grounds. A MINIATURE of the castle that CONTAINS the castle. The scale relationship is recursive. The castle contains a model of itself that leads back to itself. Waluigi refuses to think about this too hard.

points_of_interest.name: Ghostly Lobby
points_of_interest.description: Purple-hued, simplified, based on 'Luigi's Ghostly Quest.' Contains a black painting leading to MIPS's Forest. A lobby designed for ghosts, referencing Luigi's ghost-hunting adventures. This is the castle's HAUNTED lobby—the version that the dead use.

points_of_interest.name: Aquarium Lobby
points_of_interest.description: Small lobby with aquarium walls. A warp hole in the wall transports visitors INTO one of the aquariums for a green Power Star. You can be INSIDE the aquarium. The glass is not a boundary—it is a portal. Every aquarium in this castle may be a potential dimensional access point.

points_of_interest.name: Bowser's Castle
points_of_interest.description: Bowser's own version of the castle interior, with red-tinted cloud murals and Goombas. A Toad gives a Power Star during NIGHTTIME ONLY—a spy operating under cover of darkness. A star door requiring 33 Power Stars guards a tall chamber where wall-jumping reaches a balcony leading to a second, hidden entrance to Forest Maze. Bowser's Castle has SECRET EXITS that even Bowser may not know about.

points_of_interest.name: Crumbling Castle
points_of_interest.description: The castle FALLING APART over time. Entered from Sunny Balcony, the area begins intact and progressively deteriorates. Each room is more damaged than the last. This is not a corrupted state—this is ENTROPY. The castle aging, decaying, collapsing. If the Celestial Alignment fails or the Star Core is misused, THIS may be the castle's future. A green Power Star sits behind a crumbled wall with a door lying on its side—a reward for witnessing the castle's death.

points_of_interest.name: lobby.n64 & lobby.n64 (beta)
points_of_interest.description: Two stripped-down lobby variants with single painting rooms. The names reference file extensions—.n64—as if these lobbies are DATA FILES rather than physical spaces. lobby.n64 is accessed from Bowser's Domain; its beta variant has a random chance of appearing when entering the castle from Castle Grounds. The castle occasionally substitutes a SIMPLIFIED VERSION of itself when you enter. Your home has a random chance of being replaced with a bare-bones replica.

sections.name: Castle Grounds
sections.subtitle: Seven Skies Over One Castle
sections.overview:
The exterior of Peach's Castle exists in at least SEVEN confirmed states simultaneously. Waluigi has verified: Daytime, Nighttime, Sunset, Fabricated, Deadly, Inverted, and Monochrome variants of the Castle Grounds are all accessible, and the castle randomly selects which version to present based on the time of day, the traveler's Power Star count, and what appears to be architectural MOOD.

The default Castle Grounds are bright and sunny—a moat surrounding the front of the castle, fed by a waterfall and spilling into a pond. Behind the castle, a courtyard contains the giant golden Toad statue in front of Toad's Lobby. Yoshi stands near a cave in the wall and on the roof. A Wing Cap box hides behind a window on the back of the castle, and a secret passageway behind the clock face on the castle's front conceals a Bob-omb NPC.

Most warps are INACTIVE until the traveler has collected a red Power Star. The castle's exterior security system requires proof of cosmic energy before it grants full access. Walk up to the front doors without sufficient power, and you might enter Beta Lobby A through the left door or Beta Lobby E through the right. The SAME set of doors leads to DIFFERENT lobbies depending on which side you use. The castle is making decisions about your experience before you even step inside.

The back doors lead to Crescent Castle—the shadow twin. The door on the balcony across from the waterfall leads to Silent Hall—the soundless corridor. Swimming under the bridge reaches Genesis Lobby. A cave behind the castle leads to Dark Hallway. Going out of bounds near the pond leads to Eel Graveyard. The castle has MORE exits and entrances than any building should physically support.

subsections.name: The Seven Ground States
subsections.description: Each variant of the Castle Grounds represents a different state of reality, and the transitions between them are not always voluntary.

points_of_interest.name: Night Grounds
points_of_interest.description: Dark blue skybox, black trees, full moon. The moat is DRAINED, the waterfall and pond are missing. Yoshi is gone. The secret hallway behind the clock face is missing. The Wing Cap box is gone. Going out of bounds KILLS the traveler and sends them to Beta Basement. At night, the castle strips away resources and adds lethal consequences for exploration. The castle is more DANGEROUS after dark.

points_of_interest.name: Sunset Grounds
points_of_interest.description: Golden sunset ambiance with dark mauve skybox. Yoshi absent. The Wing Cap box is replaced with an empty yellow box—the resource was REMOVED, leaving only the container. Frequently accessed from Beta Lobby D, suggesting the sunset state is associated with the castle's earlier temporal configurations. The sunset is perpetual—this version of the castle is frozen at dusk.

points_of_interest.name: Deadly Grounds
points_of_interest.description: Black skybox, red lighting, decapitated Toad statue, incessant merry-go-round music. No NPCs. Toad's Lobby is GONE. The moat is drained. A star door on the castle roof requires ALL 13 red Power Stars to open, revealing a warp pipe to 'Randomized Realm.' This is the castle at its most hostile—a version where something terrible has happened. The decapitated Toad statue is a MESSAGE, and the merry-go-round music playing in a hellscape is either irony or the castle's idea of humor. Waluigi does not find it funny.

points_of_interest.name: Inverted Grounds
points_of_interest.description: Inverted color palette, missing elements, walled-up doors. The Toad statue replaced with a warp pipe to Vanilla Basement (Maze). The castle UPSIDE DOWN in every way except gravity. Accessible from Red Hallway, Purple Hallway, Parallel Lobby, and Crescent Castle. Multiple paths lead to the inverted version, suggesting it's not an anomaly but a PARALLEL STANDARD—the castle's mirror image, always present.

points_of_interest.name: Fabricated Grounds
points_of_interest.description: Resembles the castle as seen in 1995 Shoshinkai demo footage, but darker. Only two working warps. A warp hole under the bridge leads to Wet-Dry Moat. This is the castle's PROTOTYPE exterior, preserved as an accessible state. The castle remembers what it looked like before it was finished.

points_of_interest.name: Monochrome Grounds
points_of_interest.description: All color removed, gray fog, most objects gone. Toad's Lobby missing. Only the front doors work. This is a POST-GAME area, accessible only after specific conditions are met. The castle reveals this stripped-down version of itself AFTER the main story—as if removing all the decoration to show you the bare structure beneath. Or as if the castle is DYING and losing its ability to render color.

points_of_interest.name: Monochrome Grounds (Dark)
points_of_interest.description: Night falls on the colorless castle. The back doors are lying on the ground—knocked off their hinges. The doorway they once sealed now leads to 'Victorious Consequences.' Something BROKE those doors open. Something that was inside wanted out, or something outside forced its way in. This is the castle's most final state—colorless, dark, and breached.

sections.name: Courtyards
sections.subtitle: Seven Gardens of Diverging Reality
sections.overview:
The castle's courtyard system is as dimensionally fractured as everything else. Waluigi has confirmed SEVEN distinct courtyard variants, each representing a different state of the castle's exterior spaces. The courtyards are interconnected through a system that Waluigi can only describe as MOOD-BASED ARCHITECTURE—entering the fountain in one variant switches to another, collecting stars triggers state changes, and standing on the wrong statue in the wrong courtyard might send you to a crimson hellscape.

The peaceful courtyard resembles the standard castle courtyard but with a critical addition: climbing over the back wall reveals a MAZE separating Peach's Castle from an ALTERNATE VERSION made of gray stone. Two castles. One courtyard. A maze between them. The alternate castle leads to 'Funhouse'—a name that suggests entertainment, but Waluigi suspects the 'fun' is exclusively for the castle.

MIPS—the rabbit that roams the castle—can be caught in the peaceful courtyard alcove for Power Stars at 15 and 50 stars. A rabbit. In a courtyard. Carrying cosmic energy. Running from anyone who tries to catch it. Waluigi relates to MIPS on a spiritual level.

subsections.name: The Seven Courtyard States
subsections.description: Each courtyard variant can be understood as a different emotional or temporal state of the castle's exterior garden spaces.

points_of_interest.name: Peaceful Courtyard
points_of_interest.description: Haunted by Boos but otherwise calm. The Big Boo is missing, the star monument absent from the fountain. Behind the back wall: a maze with an alternate gray castle leading to Funhouse. Entering the fountain switches to the windy variant. Collecting the red coin star switches to sunny. The courtyard responds to your ACTIONS.

points_of_interest.name: Windy Courtyard
points_of_interest.description: Darker, windswept, Boos gone. The fountain holds the star monument but is dry. Peach's castle looks different—door set far back. A maze connects to the back wall. Within the maze, a monument on a platform behind a differently-textured wall warps to 'Checkerboard' with 30+ stars. WIND in a courtyard means something in this castle—atmospheric anomalies indicating dimensional instability.

points_of_interest.name: Crimson Courtyard
points_of_interest.description: A mostly empty square with red carpet, dry fountain, missing star monument, dark red haze. Accessible from Hallway and the Upstairs prohibition sign. Entering the fountain switches to windy variant. The CRIMSON designation implies blood, danger, or corruption. This is the courtyard in its most hostile state.

points_of_interest.name: Sunny Courtyard
points_of_interest.description: Sunset ambiance, no enemies. The maze walls are flowered hedges with NO COLLISION—you can walk through them. Both castle doors are walled over. A warp pipe in the alcove above Peach's castle door leads to Floor 3B. Standing in front of the alternate castle's door KILLS you and sends you to Beta Basement. Beauty concealing lethality.

points_of_interest.name: Vanilla Courtyard
points_of_interest.description: Mixture of standard and vanilla aesthetics. Star monument missing from fountain. Only the Big Boo remains. Defeating it drops a cage to Big Boo's Haunt (beta). The castle door leads to Dream Basement. This courtyard is the castle REMEMBERING its original state—imperfectly.

points_of_interest.name: Ghostly Courtyard
points_of_interest.description: Dry fountain with a Boo STATUE in the middle. No trees, no grass. Standing on the Boo statue warps to the crimson courtyard. The Boo statue is a PORTAL disguised as decoration. Lower door leads to Aventura Lobby, upper door to Sanctuary, back door to Ghostly Upstairs.

points_of_interest.name: Fabricated Courtyard
points_of_interest.description: Primitive recreation with darker textures. A WELL replaces the fountain—wells being traditional portals to underworlds. Entering the well kills you and sends you to Beta Basement. The Big Boo drops a cage to 'Big Boo's Memory'—not Big Boo's Haunt, but Big Boo's MEMORY. The ghost carries memories rather than haunting a mansion. A warp hole in the ground leads to Fabricated Checkerboard.

points_of_interest.name: Bloody Courtyard
points_of_interest.description: Similar to crimson variant but the fountain is filled with BLOOD and the 'Eternal Star/L Is Real 2401' plinth is replaced with L himself. Accessible through Challenge Lobby's walled-up door (via Vanish Cap) and His Domain's final room. This is the castle's most disturbing exterior state—whatever happened here left the fountain running with blood and a mystery standing where a riddle used to be.

sections.name: Gardens & Greenhouses
sections.subtitle: Controlled Nature in Uncontrolled Space
sections.overview:
Scattered throughout the castle complex are garden spaces that represent attempts to impose ORDER on the castle's chaotic architecture. These are places where someone—Toads, presumably—tried to create peaceful natural environments within the dimensional madness. The results are mixed.

The Castle Garden behind Beta Basement contains trees, flowerbeds, and Goombas—a functional garden that serves as a transition space. A Toad House appears here after collecting 120 stars, leading to Toad's Rec Room. The Toads built themselves a VACATION SPOT in the shadow of a haunted temporal archive. Waluigi respects the audacity.

The Greenhouse Framework is an enclosed garden with grid walls that reveal the Wet-Dry World skybox beyond. The greenhouse exists in a space where normal reality ENDS and the Wet-Dry dimension BEGINS. Growing flowers at the edge of a flooded alternate reality is either brave gardening or dimensional agriculture.

subsections.name: Garden Spaces
subsections.description: Each garden serves a different function within the castle's ecosystem.

points_of_interest.name: Castle Garden
points_of_interest.description: Large enclosed garden behind Beta Basement with trees, flowerbeds, and a warp pipe to Toad's Hedge Maze. The 120-star Toad House suggests the Toads have a SECRET RECREATION FACILITY that only unlocks after maximum power accumulation. The gardeners have been hiding a break room.

points_of_interest.name: Greenhouse Framework
points_of_interest.description: Enclosed garden with grid walls showing the Wet-Dry World skybox. Contains a silver Toad statue, water features, and connections to Basement, Basement Maze, Internal Garden, and Parallel Lobby. The silver Toad statue contrasts with the golden one in Toad's Lobby—different metals, different significance, different eras of memorial.

points_of_interest.name: Internal Garden
points_of_interest.description: Large interior garden with a Luigi painting that triggers character switching and a Bowser laugh. A mirror divides the corridor to the painting—bypassed with the Vanish Cap. The Luigi painting is DARK compared to other portraits. Entering it doesn't just warp you—it CHANGES WHO YOU ARE and lets Bowser mock you for it. The garden is beautiful. The painting is psychological warfare.

points_of_interest.name: Warped Internal Garden
points_of_interest.description: Small enclosed garden with a treacherous pit. Walking on the roof via treetops reaches Dark Maze. A window hides a warp to Floor 4B—entering the pit ALSO leads to Floor 4B. Two paths to the same destination: one requiring skill and exploration, the other requiring falling into a trap. The castle rewards both competence and failure with the same result.

points_of_interest.name: Goomba Garden
points_of_interest.description: Small L-shaped outdoor area connecting Enhanced Underground and Vanilla Basement (Maze). Dry fountain, wandering Goombas. A TRANSITIONAL garden—a brief moment of open sky between two underground horrors. The Goombas don't seem to mind.

points_of_interest.name: Piranha Plant Garden
points_of_interest.description: A hazy plain with floating islands, cannons, a mountain with a spike, and Piranha Plant statues. A warp pipe beside a GIANT Piranha Plant statue leads to Piranha's Igloo. The garden has been CLAIMED by Piranha Plants—their statues mark territory. This is not a garden maintained for visitors. This is a garden that has been CONQUERED by its plants.

points_of_interest.name: Garden (Simple)
points_of_interest.description: Castle walls surrounding a small peaceful area with sunset lighting, two trees, and a Peach stained glass window. Connects Aquarium Lobby and Tower Pinnacle. The simplest garden in the entire castle—almost suspiciously simple. In a castle where every space hides dimensions within dimensions, a genuinely peaceful garden feels like a trap. Waluigi trusts nothing.

sections.name: Upper Floors
sections.subtitle: Ascent Through Mirrors and Madness
sections.overview:
The castle's upper floors are accessed through spiral staircases, key doors, and dimensional transitions. Six confirmed upstairs areas exist, each representing a different architectural philosophy—or a different PERSONALITY of the castle. The upper floors share one common feature: MIRRORS. Mirrors that can be passed through with the Vanish Cap, mirrors that show different reflections than expected, mirrors that serve as portals between versions of reality.

Waluigi notes that mirrors in dimensional architecture are not decorative. A mirror is a boundary between two states—the real and the reflected. In a castle where multiple realities coexist, a mirror is a DOOR. The castle's architects understood this and placed mirrors at strategic transition points throughout the upper floors.

The 'endless' stairs appear in multiple upstairs areas. In some, they are genuinely endless—looping infinitely. In others, they lead to specific destinations. The stairs are SELECTIVE. They decide whether you can ascend based on criteria that Waluigi has not been able to fully determine. Star count matters. But Waluigi suspects the stairs also evaluate something less quantifiable.

subsections.name: The Six Upstairs Variants
subsections.description: Each upstairs area serves as a different layer of the castle's vertical structure, with increasing strangeness as you ascend.

points_of_interest.name: Vanilla Upstairs
points_of_interest.description: Resembles the standard upper floor but with critical differences: most warps lead to BETA versions of vanilla stages. The mirror room's Vanish Cap allows passing through the mirror to Mirrored Upstairs. The starry sky painting is a working warp. The clock's glass can be broken to access Clockwork Innards via the pendulum. The 'endless' stairs are NOT endless—they lead to a grated warp hole. The castle has UNLOCKED its own staircase restriction.

points_of_interest.name: Mirrored Upstairs
points_of_interest.description: EVERYTHING IS REVERSED. All paintings are backwards. The Bob-omb Battlefield painting appears where no painting exists in the normal version. The starry night walls are PINK instead of blue. A faceless Toad gives a Power Star—another faceless entity dispensing cosmic energy. All painting warps lead to reversed or corrupted versions of their normal destinations. This is the castle's REFLECTION—not a copy, but a mirror image where left is right and normal is wrong.

points_of_interest.name: Purple Upstairs
points_of_interest.description: Purple-tinted version with an attached lobby. The Tiny-Huge Island room is replaced with stairs to Ghostly Lobby—the GHOST entrance replaces the scale-manipulation room. The 'endless' stairs work normally but lead to Kuppa1—the ORIGINAL Bowser battle. The clock bears the beta face from Castle Grounds. This upstairs preserves an earlier version of the castle's vertical hierarchy.

points_of_interest.name: Ghostly Upstairs
points_of_interest.description: Purple-hued, based on 'Luigi's Ghostly Quest.' Contains a central room, circular hallway, mirror room (with enemy Lakitu carrying a camera ON THE OTHER SIDE), courtyard room, and sand-floored rooms. The Vanish Cap in the first sand room allows mirror passage to Floor 4B. A Lakitu with a camera watching from inside the mirror—the castle's reflection is FILMING YOU.

points_of_interest.name: Pink Upstairs
points_of_interest.description: Mauve-colored variant without a third floor. The mirror room has NO MIRROR—the boundary has been removed. The 'endless' stairs lead to Polygonal Chaos. Connects to Solar Tower, Tower Pinnacle, Crumbling Castle, and Bowser's Domain. This upstairs has been SIMPLIFIED—fewer floors, no mirror barrier, direct connections to extreme destinations.

points_of_interest.name: Upstairs (Primary)
points_of_interest.description: Accessed from Beta Lobby B via a checkerboard hallway, available in bright and dark variants. Contains a Wet-Dry World painting, Jolly Roger Bay painting, composite Lethal Lava Land paintings (red for lava, green for grassy variant), and a sky painting on the FLOOR leading to Rainbow Ride (beta). A painting ON THE FLOOR—you don't enter it, you FALL INTO IT. The upper floor leads to a celestial area with a crescent moon door to Cryptic Hideout and doors to Corridor. Through door '3' and a hole: Ghost House painting, with Forest Maze below if you exit. Layered warps—one destination stacked above another.

sections.name: The AI Undergrounds & The Core
sections.subtitle: What Lies at the Heart
sections.overview:
At the deepest point of the castle's most corrupted floor—accessed through 4th Floor (corrupted) via a warp pipe—lies a small cluster of hallways called the AI Undergrounds. Whomps and Goombas patrol the corridors. One wall is made of brick with a section of DIFFERENT TEXTURE that can be passed through to reveal a hidden room.

Inside: a mysterious object known as the CORE.

Waluigi has very limited intelligence on the Core. It appears to be a physical manifestation of... something. Its textures GLITCH—not damaged, but actively changing, as if the object exists in multiple states simultaneously and cannot settle on a single appearance. Attempting to destroy the Core has no effect. It is either indestructible or exists in a state where physical force cannot interact with it.

Waluigi connects this to the Star Core mentioned in intelligence reports about the castle's power source. If the AI Undergrounds contain a physical interface with the Star Core—or ARE the Star Core—then Fawful's goal becomes terrifyingly clear. He is not trying to reach a power source buried beneath the castle. He is trying to reach an ENTITY that exists at the intersection of all the castle's dimensional states, hidden behind corrupted architecture and guarded by the castle's most hostile inhabitants.

The Core glitches. The castle glitches. Floor 4B corrupts. The Fabricated Lobby breaks. The Flooded Basement traps. All of these phenomena may be SYMPTOMS of the Core's influence—or the Core's CONTAINMENT failing.

The Celestial Alignment may be the moment when the Core's dimensional instability peaks and its containment becomes temporarily vulnerable. If Fawful reaches it at that moment...

Waluigi does not want to finish that thought.

WAH.

subsections.name: The Bloody Courtyard Connection
subsections.description:
The Bloody Courtyard—fountain filled with blood, L standing where the 'L Is Real' plinth used to be—is accessible from two locations: Challenge Lobby (via Vanish Cap through the walled door) and His Domain's final room. 'His Domain' connects to the trap door on Floor 2B, the sun carpet on Floor 3B, and the Bloody Courtyard. Whoever 'He' is, His Domain spans multiple basement levels and culminates in a courtyard of blood.

Waluigi suspects 'He' is connected to the Core. The Domain represents the physical territory of whatever entity the Core embodies. The bloody fountain is not decoration—it is a MARKER. 'He' has been here. 'He' has claimed this space.

The fact that L—Luigi? Someone else?—stands in the Bloody Courtyard where a riddle used to be suggests that the mystery of 'L Is Real' has been ANSWERED. And the answer is standing in a fountain of blood, waiting for someone to arrive.

Waluigi would very much like to NOT be that someone.

sections.name: The Deeper Architecture
sections.subtitle: What Lies Beyond the Known Castle
sections.overview:
Beyond the castle's basements, lobbies, courtyards, and upper floors lies a vast network of interconnected spaces that Waluigi can only describe as the castle's UNCONSCIOUS MIND. Nearly THREE HUNDRED additional areas exist within or connected to the castle complex—courses, challenges, boss arenas, test chambers, voids, and spaces that defy categorization entirely.

Waluigi has spent considerable time reviewing intelligence on these areas, and he has identified several critical categories: the Bowser Arenas (where the castle's primary antagonist stages his confrontations), the 4th Floor Complex (where the castle's most dangerous secrets converge), the Crimson Hallways (blood-red mazes that serve as the castle's immune system), the Test Areas (prototype spaces preserved from the castle's earliest construction), the Corrupted Zones (areas where dimensional integrity has failed), and the Voids (spaces where reality itself has been subtracted).

The sheer NUMBER of these areas tells a story. A castle with fifteen basements and twenty-nine lobbies is strange. A castle connected to nearly three hundred additional dimensional spaces is not a building—it is a UNIVERSE wearing the shape of a building. Every painting, every warp pipe, every suspicious floor tile is a doorway to somewhere else. The castle is not contained within its walls. Its walls are contained within IT.

WAH.

subsections.name: The 4th Floor Complex — Finding the Core
subsections.description:
The 4th Floor exists in at least FOUR confirmed states: standard, beta, final, and corrupted. Each represents a different stage in the castle's ongoing relationship with whatever lies at its heart.

The standard 4th Floor resembles the Beta Lobbies with painting rooms and a courtyard containing a Toad statue. The beta 4th Floor is a hub of warp pipes leading to test courses—prototype spaces still under construction. The 'final' 4th Floor is a deteriorating corridor leading to a room with a kitchen, a pulpit, a Mad Piano, and a golden Toad statue that, when approached, delivers a flashing message: 'FIND THE CORE.'

FIND. THE. CORE.

The castle is giving INSTRUCTIONS. It is not merely a passive structure—it is actively directing its inhabitants toward the Core. The Toad statue is a MESSENGER. The entire 4th Floor complex is a PATHWAY, designed to guide those with sufficient Power Stars toward the castle's deepest secret.

The corrupted 4th Floor—accessed by looking up at the Toad statue in the final version—is identical but bathed in darkness with slower music. Its warp pipe leads to the AI Undergrounds, where the Core itself can be found behind a false wall. Looking up at the Toad statue in the corrupted version kills you and sends you to Beta Basement. The statue REWARDS you in one state and PUNISHES you in another. The castle is testing whether you approach from the right direction.

points_of_interest.name: The 4th Floor (Final) — Kitchen & Pulpit
points_of_interest.description: A kitchen with cake. A wooden pulpit. A Mad Piano. A Toad. A balcony. A garden with a golden Toad statue. This reads like a HOUSEHOLD—living quarters for whoever maintained the castle's deepest level. The pulpit suggests religious or ceremonial functions. The Mad Piano suggests that even domestic spaces in this castle are hostile. The cake in the kitchen may be connected to the 'Delicious Cake' dimension accessible elsewhere.

points_of_interest.name: The 'FIND THE CORE' Message
points_of_interest.description: A golden Toad statue that flashes 'FIND THE CORE' when approached. This is the castle's most direct communication with its inhabitants. No riddles, no puzzles—a simple imperative. The castle WANTS someone to find the Core. The question is: does it want someone to find the Core to PROTECT it, to USE it, or to DESTROY it?

points_of_interest.name: The AI Undergrounds Path
points_of_interest.description: Corrupted 4th Floor → warp pipe → AI Undergrounds → false wall → The Core. This is the castle's FINAL APPROACH. To reach the Core, you must: navigate the castle's lobby network, descend through multiple basement levels, reach the 4th Floor, trigger the corrupted state, survive the underground hallways patrolled by Whomps and Goombas, and identify the false wall. The castle has made the Core difficult but NOT impossible to reach. It is a TEST, not a lockout.

subsections.name: Bowser's Territory
subsections.description:
Bowser has established multiple strongholds within the castle complex, each representing a different aspect of his occupation. Waluigi counts at least TEN Bowser-related battle arenas and territory areas, suggesting Bowser did not merely invade the castle—he INTEGRATED himself into its dimensional structure.

Bowser in the Dark World, Bowser in the Fire Sea, Bowser in the Volcano, Bowser in the Castle, Bowser in the Sub, Bowser in the Airship Cabin—six distinct battle arenas, each in a different environment. Bowser doesn't fight in one location. He fights EVERYWHERE. His combat spaces span darkness, fire, volcanic chambers, castle interiors, submarines, and airships. He has adapted his warfare to every terrain the castle offers.

Bowser's Domain is his headquarters within the castle: a dark, illusory area with a main hall, a PRISON holding faceless Toads and Bob-omb Buddies, a bedroom with an enormous bed and a photo of the castle, and a basement maze with water-filled grooves. The bedroom is particularly telling—Bowser SLEEPS in the castle. He has made it his HOME. The photo of the castle on his nightstand suggests he views the castle with something approaching affection. Or possessiveness.

Bowser's Floor is the FUTURE version of Peach's Floor—the castle after Bowser has taken control. A bronze Toad statue replaces features. Hallways are haunted by Boos. A walled-up doorway suggests areas that Bowser deliberately sealed. This is what the castle looks like under Bowser's rule—recognizable but WRONG.

points_of_interest.name: Bowser's Prison
points_of_interest.description: T-shaped hallways holding cells with Toads, Bob-omb Buddies, and Yoshis. A throne room with a giant throne. Standing on the throne warps to Peach's Floor—the pre-Bowser version. Bowser's throne is a TIME MACHINE. Sitting on it takes you to the past, to when Peach still ruled. Does Bowser sit on his throne and look at what he conquered? Or what he destroyed?

points_of_interest.name: The Faceless Toad Prisoner
points_of_interest.description: In Bowser's Domain's prison, a faceless Toad sits in a cell with a breakable block hiding a warp to Escape Route. Using the Vanish Cap to enter his cell and speaking to him yields a Power Star. Another faceless entity—stripped of identity, imprisoned, but still carrying cosmic energy. The faceless Toads throughout the castle may all be the SAME entity, scattered across dimensional states.

points_of_interest.name: Bob-omb Village & Dead Village
points_of_interest.description: Accessible from Bowser's Floor, Bob-omb Village is a pleasant community with hostile undertones. Taking certain actions drains the village's energy, transforming it into Dead Village—an icy wasteland where only one house remains. The sole surviving house's occupant is MISSING. The village's destruction is not Bowser's doing—it is triggered by the VISITOR collecting a Power Star. The castle punishes those who take from its communities.

subsections.name: The Crimson Hallways — The Castle's Immune System
subsections.description:
Two versions of the Crimson Hallway exist as Areas 1 and 14, identical in layout but with different death consequences. Both consist of a circular room, a maze haunted by a Big Boo, and a vertical shaft—all bathed in crimson fog with floating chairs.

Waluigi theorizes that the Crimson Hallways are the castle's IMMUNE SYSTEM. They connect critical areas (Beta Lobby C, Beta Basement, the Courtyard, Aquarium Limbo) while punishing unauthorized travelers with death warps. Dying in Area 1 always sends you to Beta Basement. Dying in Area 14 during 'ACT 1' sends you to Monochrome Castle Grounds (dark)—the castle's most final state.

The key doors in the maze lead to Bowser in the Castle—where a Bowser battle yields a red Power Star that is the SAME star as Kuppa1. The stars share an ID. Collecting one marks the other as collected. Two battles in different locations for the SAME cosmic energy. The castle treats these encounters as a single event occurring in two places simultaneously.

points_of_interest.name: The Shared Star ID
points_of_interest.description: Bowser in the Castle and Kuppa1 share a red Power Star ID. This means the castle considers these two battles—in different locations, against different versions of Bowser—to be the SAME BATTLE. Cosmic energy does not distinguish between dimensional instances.

points_of_interest.name: The ACT 1 Death Consequence
points_of_interest.description: Dying in Crimson Hallway Area 14 during 'ACT 1' warps to the dark Monochrome Castle Grounds—the final state where the back doors have been broken open. Death in the crimson maze during a specific narrative state leads to the castle's ENDING. The Crimson Hallways are not just pathways—they are NARRATIVE CHECKPOINTS.

subsections.name: Preserved Test Areas
subsections.description:
The castle preserves prototype testing spaces from its earliest construction: 'athletic' (a geometric concrete mountain for movement testing), 'castle' (a structure with a fake star that triggers a dimensional shift to its expanded variant), 'castle2' through 'castle4' (progressively more complex test structures), and 'Collision Test' (a plane of colored squares forming the number '33').

The number 33 appears in the Collision Test area and in the castle's name conventions. 33 Power Stars are required for certain star doors. The number may represent a threshold—a critical mass of cosmic energy required to access specific states of the castle. Or it may be a signature. The architects of this place left the number 33 embedded in their test infrastructure, like an artist signing their work.

These test areas are not relics. They are ACTIVE. They contain Power Stars. They connect to the castle's transit network. The castle's prototype spaces were never decommissioned—they were incorporated into the final structure as functional components. The testing never ended. The castle is STILL being tested.

points_of_interest.name: The Athletic Test Area
points_of_interest.description: A geometric concrete mountain in a sky-blue void, originally for testing movement on various terrain types. The varying terrains and colors are missing in the current version—stripped back to bare geometry. The castle preserved the SHAPE of the test but removed its PURPOSE. A skeleton of intent.

points_of_interest.name: The Castle Stage Dimensional Shift
points_of_interest.description: A structure with a blue platform at the top holding what appears to be a Power Star. Approaching it triggers a shift to 'variant B'—a greatly expanded version. The fake star is BAIT. The castle uses deception to trigger dimensional transitions. Approaching a reward triggers a punishment (dimensional displacement). But the REAL reward is in variant B. The castle teaches through trickery.

points_of_interest.name: The 33 Signature
points_of_interest.description: The number 33 formed from raised platforms in Collision Test. B3313. 33 stars for star doors. The number is everywhere. Whoever built this castle—or whatever force shaped it—considers 33 to be significant. In numerology, 33 is a 'master number' associated with spiritual uplift and guidance. The castle may be designed not just as a structure but as a SPIRITUAL INSTRUMENT.

subsections.name: The Voids & Liminal Spaces
subsections.description:
Several areas within the castle complex consist of NOTHING—empty spaces where reality has been subtracted rather than constructed. The Bob-omb Void contains only Prince Bob-omb's mangled body, his arms rearranged grotesquely. The Crusher is a small checkerboard in blackness that kills the visitor. Aquarium Limbo is a red-tinted aquarium leading to a long tunnel.

These voids are not empty by accident. They are spaces where reality has been REMOVED. Something was here and is now gone—or something was here and CONSUMED the surroundings. The voids may be the castle's version of scar tissue: places where dimensional damage occurred and the surrounding reality collapsed inward.

The Behind the Stained Glass area deserves special attention. After defeating Bowser in the Castle, the visitor spawns behind the Princess Peach stained glass window and encounters Peach's APPARITION. She calls Mario's name, leads the visitor down a hallway, vanishes when approached, reappears in a vertical shaft, and finally guides them to the back of the stained glass window itself. Peach's ghost is a GUIDE—she leads visitors through a specific path behind her own memorial. The dead princess is giving tours of the space behind her own portrait.

If the Peach Loyalists knew about this, Captain Toadette would NEVER leave this castle.

points_of_interest.name: Prince Bob-omb's Void
points_of_interest.description: An empty void containing only the mangled body of Prince Bob-omb—arms removed, one protruding from his crown. This is not a battle site. This is an AFTERMATH. Someone—or something—destroyed the prince and left his body in a void as a display. The arm emerging from the crown suggests his own power was turned against him.

points_of_interest.name: Peach's Ghost Tour
points_of_interest.description: Behind the Stained Glass: Peach's apparition appears, calls Mario's name, leads visitors through hallways and a vertical shaft, and guides them to the back of her own stained glass window—which exits to Vanilla Castle Grounds. The ghost of the murdered princess has PROGRAMMED A ROUTE through the castle. She is not a random haunting. She is a NAVIGATION SYSTEM.

points_of_interest.name: Above the Clouds
points_of_interest.description: Located on the castle's roof at nighttime, with a rainbow bridge leading to a higher tower. Accessible only through 'Judgment' with 33+ Power Stars. The castle's HIGHEST point requires cosmic accumulation and moral evaluation ('Judgment') to reach. This is the castle's ASCENSION—the opposite of the basement descent. At the bottom: the Core. At the top: the clouds. The castle spans from the depths of reality to its heights.

points_of_interest.name: Beginnings
points_of_interest.description: A red and white checkerboard plane with a sky blue background, a warp pipe, and a sign. Only appears after defeating the final Bowser. Inspired by 1995 demo footage showing Luigi with Mario. The sign references a missing brother. This is the castle's ORIGIN POINT—the state before everything else was built. After completing the castle's challenges, you return to the BEGINNING. The castle is a LOOP.

subsections.name: The Castle's Living Spaces
subsections.description:
Scattered throughout the hundreds of connected areas are spaces that suggest the castle was not just a government building or a dimensional nexus—it was a HOME. People LIVED here. They cooked, they slept, they bathed, they gardened, they played.

The Bros' House contains two beds—one with red bedclothes, one with green. Mario and Luigi's bedroom. A downstairs room with a table and a box containing a green Power Star. The house is accessible from Floor 4B and Waterfall, suggesting it exists in a pocket dimension between the castle's deepest basement and a natural landmark. The brothers' home is literally between the castle's most dangerous level and a waterfall.

The Castle Bathroom features showers where Toads are bathing. TOADS. SHOWERING. In a castle that contains dimensional horrors, temporal paradoxes, and the ghosts of murdered princesses, the Toads still take showers. Waluigi finds this simultaneously the most normal and most surreal detail in the entire castle.

Blasting Bullet Factory reveals that Bowser had an INDUSTRIAL OPERATION manufacturing silver Bullet Bills. A Bob-omb Buddy serves as factory foreman, toasted orange by the heat, complaining about production being down. Even in a factory of war, someone is worried about their quarterly output.

points_of_interest.name: The Bros' House
points_of_interest.description: Two beds. Red and green. A table. A Power Star in a box. This is where the heroes LIVED—between a floor of dimensional labyrinth and a waterfall. Home is a pocket dimension. Waluigi does not have a house. Waluigi lives in a van. The plumbers have a house inside a transdimensional castle. Life is not fair.

points_of_interest.name: The Showering Toads
points_of_interest.description: Castle Bathroom. Showers. Toads bathing. Connected to Bowser's Domain on one side and Peaceful Grounds on the other. The Toads shower between Bowser's headquarters and a peaceful garden. Hygiene persists even in dimensional chaos.

points_of_interest.name: The Bullet Bill Factory
points_of_interest.description: Self-destruct mode triggered by intruders. Rising and falling lava. A vault. A secret aquarium. An orange Bob-omb Buddy complaining about production quotas. Bowser ran a MILITARY-INDUSTRIAL COMPLEX inside the castle, complete with middle management. Waluigi suspects there are performance reviews filed somewhere in the castle's archives.

points_of_interest.name: Ancient City
points_of_interest.description: A temple guarded by a Bob-omb Buddy overlooking a walled city with dry fountains. FLOODING the city by entering the temple against the guardian's wishes destroys all inhabitants except the Bob-omb, who is 'none too pleased.' An entire CIVILIZATION accessible through a Nocturnal Lobby painting, destroyable by the visitor's actions. The castle contains cities that can be KILLED.

sections.name: The Dimensional Catalog
sections.subtitle: A World Inside Every Painting
sections.overview:
Waluigi has attempted to catalog the nearly three hundred dimensional spaces accessible from within or connected to Peach's Castle. The task is overwhelming. Every painting is a portal. Every warp pipe is a highway. Every suspicious floor tile might deposit you in a volcanic factory, an underwater graveyard, a haunted mansion, a flesh-covered mountain, or a checkerboard floating in an infinite void.

What follows is Waluigi's analysis of the most strategically significant, narratively relevant, or deeply disturbing spaces he has identified. This is not a complete catalog—a complete catalog would require its own encyclopedia. This is a SURVIVAL GUIDE for anyone foolish enough to explore this castle.

Waluigi wants to emphasize: the castle is connected to EVERYTHING. Snow fields, lava lakes, underwater cities, floating hotels, haunted forests, military factories, ancient temples, flesh mountains, cake dimensions, and at least one area that is literally just a bathroom where Toads shower. The castle is not a building with rooms. It is a SWITCHBOARD connecting every conceivable environment, and many inconceivable ones.

WAH.

subsections.name: The Core — What Everyone Is Looking For
subsections.description:
The Core appears in three distinct locations within the castle complex: the AI Undergrounds (accessed through 4th Floor corrupted), Core Maze (accessed through Flesh Mountain or Personalization Chamber), and Core Maze (beta) (also through Personalization Chamber). In all locations, the Core is the same: a mysterious object with glitching textures that cannot be destroyed.

The 4th Floor (final) displays a flashing message—'FIND THE CORE'—when the golden Toad statue is approached. The castle is not subtle about this. It WANTS someone to find the Core. The entire 4th Floor complex exists as a pathway to this discovery.

Waluigi's theory: the Core is not merely a power source. It is the castle's HEART—the dimensional anchor point from which all the castle's reality-warping effects emanate. The Star Core referenced in intelligence reports about continental barriers may be the same entity viewed from a different dimensional perspective. The Core glitches because it exists in ALL of the castle's dimensional states simultaneously. It is the one thing that is present in every version of the castle—the constant around which everything else rotates.

If Fawful reaches the Core during the Celestial Alignment, he would not merely access a power source. He would access the FOUNDATION OF REALITY for the entire Mushroom Kingdom.

subsections.name: Military & Industrial Zones
subsections.description: The castle connects to multiple military and industrial facilities, revealing that someone has been manufacturing weapons and staging battles within the dimensional network.

points_of_interest.name: Blasting Bullet Factory
points_of_interest.description: An active weapons factory manufacturing silver Bullet Bills for Bowser. Features: self-destruct mode (rising lava), a vault, a secret aquarium, and an orange Bob-omb Buddy serving as factory foreman who complains about missing management and ruined production. The factory has MIDDLE MANAGEMENT. Bowser's military-industrial complex includes performance reviews and quarterly targets. Accessible from Nebula Lobby.

points_of_interest.name: Battle Fort
points_of_interest.description: A cage-like arena crawling with enemies. A Chuckya guards a Power Star on the catwalk. This is a GLADIATORIAL ARENA—enemies confined in a cage, visitors fighting through them for cosmic energy. Accessible from the peaceful Courtyard, of all places.

points_of_interest.name: Eternal Fort & Eternal Fort (Beta)
points_of_interest.description: Bowser's FINAL stronghold—two versions of the same fortress where the last battle occurs. The standard version requires traversing a gauntlet of enemies before facing Bowser with Bullet Bill Blasters. The beta version is simpler but features a two-floor battle. Both yield the same jumbo yellow Power Star (shared ID), and both lead to Beginnings—the castle's origin point. Defeating Bowser sends you BACK TO THE START. The castle is a loop.

points_of_interest.name: Ice-Cold Warzone
points_of_interest.description: Accessible through Dark Downtown via a warp pipe. Collecting the Power Star here warps to Bob-omb's Revenge—a desolate battlefield where Prince Bob-omb waits with a timer counting upward. War zones leading to revenge scenarios. The castle preserves the CONSEQUENCES of conflict.

subsections.name: The Haunted Network
subsections.description: An entire subset of the castle's connected spaces is dedicated to ghosts, death, and the boundary between existence and non-existence.

points_of_interest.name: Big Boo's Memory vs. Big Boo's Haunt (Beta)
points_of_interest.description: Two versions of the haunted mansion: one is a BETA (simplified but functional version accessed from Vanilla Courtyard), the other is a MEMORY (accessed from Fabricated Courtyard). The distinction matters. A beta is an earlier version. A memory is a RECOLLECTION. Big Boo's Memory is what the mansion REMEMBERS about itself—a simplified recreation where many rooms are completely empty. The ghosts remember the structure but have forgotten the details.

points_of_interest.name: Ghost House (via Upstairs)
points_of_interest.description: Named after the development codename for Big Boo's Haunt. Features a library, a mirror with Luigi's reflection regardless of which character you're using, and a door under a large 'L' that switches your character to Luigi. The mirror always shows LUIGI. Even when Mario looks, he sees Luigi. The castle's haunted spaces associate mirrors with identity crisis.

points_of_interest.name: Eel Graveyard
points_of_interest.description: An underwater area where Unagi eels appear to be dead—until approached, when textures glitch and the eels spring to life, flying through the ceiling and out of bounds. The 'dead' are not dead. They are DORMANT. Disturbing them causes dimensional instability (glitching textures) and escape beyond the area's boundaries. A metaphor for the castle's relationship with death: nothing stays dead, and resurrection causes reality to break.

points_of_interest.name: Bob-omb Void
points_of_interest.description: An empty void containing Prince Bob-omb's mangled body—arms removed, one protruding from his crown. Accessed through bob.n64 via a suspicious flowerbed. Someone or something destroyed Bob-omb royalty and displayed the body in a dimension of NOTHING. This is either a warning, a punishment, or a trophy.

points_of_interest.name: Dead Village
points_of_interest.description: Bob-omb Village after its Power Star is collected—an icy wasteland where only one house remains and its occupant is MISSING. The act of collecting a star DESTROYED a community. Cosmic energy extraction has consequences. The Toads binding Power Stars to their dead in the catacombs may have understood this—removing bound energy destroys what it was bound to.

subsections.name: Wet-Dry World & The Flooded Cities
subsections.description: The Wet-Dry World dimension is one of the castle's most extensively developed connected spaces, featuring multiple versions of the same fundamental concept: CITIES that can be DROWNED.

points_of_interest.name: Dry Town / Flooded Town
points_of_interest.description: Two versions of the same town, accessible through the same painting depending on the basement's flooding state. They have significant STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES—they are not the same area at different water levels. They are PARALLEL VERSIONS of the same city in different dimensional states. The town features a Cloud House from Rainbow Ride (with a working fireplace that survives flooding), crystal taps for water control, and a Bob-omb NPC with dialogue from another ROM hack entirely. Even the NPCs are borrowed from other realities.

points_of_interest.name: Dark Downtown
points_of_interest.description: A flooded town where a Bob-omb Buddy in a temple claims the 'entire town' has gone mad and needs to be 'cooled down' with a flood. The SOLUTION to madness is drowning. The castle's architectural philosophy in a single NPC dialogue: when things go wrong, add water.

points_of_interest.name: Ancient City
points_of_interest.description: A two-leveled walled city with a temple guarded by a Bob-omb Buddy. Entering the temple against the guardian's wishes FLOODS THE CITY AND KILLS ALL INHABITANTS except the Bob-omb. An entire civilization destroyed because a visitor ignored a warning. The castle preserves cities that can be murdered by curiosity.

points_of_interest.name: Bridge to Wet-Dry Town
points_of_interest.description: A narrow bridge leading to a door set against the Wet-Dry World skybox—actually the Old Walled City of Shibam, Yemen. The castle's dimensional painters used a photograph of a REAL CITY as the backdrop for their flooded dimension. Reality and fiction blur. The castle's paintings reference actual places on Earth.

subsections.name: Test Areas & Preserved Prototypes
subsections.description: Numerous spaces within the castle network are explicitly labeled as test areas—prototype environments preserved from the earliest stages of construction.

points_of_interest.name: Athletic / Athletic2
points_of_interest.description: Geometric concrete structures in colored voids, originally for movement testing. Athletic is a mountain of ramps; Athletic2 is a simple wall-jump structure. The castle's PHYSICS TESTING LABS are accessible spaces containing Power Stars. You can earn cosmic energy by visiting the room where gravity was calibrated.

points_of_interest.name: Castle / Castle2 / Castle3 / Castle4
points_of_interest.description: Four test structures of increasing complexity. Castle contains a FAKE STAR that triggers a dimensional shift to an expanded variant—the castle uses deception in its test areas. Castle2 is labeled 'Moveset Test.' Castle3 is 'Course Test.' Castle4 has no label but is the most complex. The progression from 1 to 4 tells the story of the castle's development: movement testing → course design → unnamed advancement.

points_of_interest.name: Collision Test
points_of_interest.description: A plane of colored squares forming the number '33.' B3313. The number is a SIGNATURE embedded in the castle's test infrastructure. The builders signed their work with a number that would later become the castle's designation.

points_of_interest.name: Funhouse (Stage3/Donjon)
points_of_interest.description: A maze of mismatched wall textures based on a prototype castle hub called 'donjon'—Middle English for a castle keep or stronghold. Hidden doors in specific walls lead to other areas. The ORIGINAL CASTLE HUB is still accessible, preserved as a maze where finding the exits requires knowing which walls are fake. The castle's first draft is its most honest: a confusing maze where nothing matches and every surface lies.

subsections.name: Liminal & Impossible Spaces
subsections.description: Some connected spaces exist in states that challenge the concept of 'space' itself.

points_of_interest.name: Delicious Cake
points_of_interest.description: It's the cake Princess Peach promised Mario. A GIANT CAKE in a void, accessible through a Peach painting in Crescent Castle or a literal cake on Floor 3B. The unused Japanese text 'おいしいケーキ' (delicious cake) was assigned to a level containing only the end-game cake image. The cake dimension may be the castle's concept of an ENDING—a promise fulfilled, preserved as an accessible space. The cake is not a lie. The cake is a POCKET DIMENSION.

points_of_interest.name: Flesh Mountain
points_of_interest.description: A mountain with a red 'waterfall' flowing from a cave. The cave leads to Core Maze. The FLESH designation is not metaphorical—the mountain's texture suggests organic material. The path to the Core passes through something that is ALIVE. The castle's deepest secret is accessed through living tissue.

points_of_interest.name: Checker boards
points_of_interest.description: Multiple checkerboard planes exist in infinite voids—Checkerboard, Fabricated Checkerboard, Beginnings. Each contains a Power Star in the distance. These are the castle's MINIMAL SPACES—reality reduced to a grid pattern and a point of cosmic energy. The checkerboard is the castle's fundamental unit of reality: order (the pattern) and purpose (the star) in otherwise empty existence.

points_of_interest.name: Crusher
points_of_interest.description: A small checkerboard in a black void. Stepping on it triggers an unseen force that CRUSHES the visitor. The simplest space in the castle is also one of the most lethal. Accessible from Floor 4B's aquarium room. The castle hides death in minimalism.

points_of_interest.name: Endless Fun / Endings
points_of_interest.description: The castle's FINAL destinations. Endings: a green checkerboard with a jumbo red Power Star, requiring 459 stars to access. Endless Fun: a black void with a faceless Toad who addresses the player. After collecting everything, the castle shows you a faceless entity in NOTHING. 459 stars of accumulated cosmic energy lead to a conversation with no face in no place. The castle's ultimate reward is an encounter with identity-less existence.

points_of_interest.name: The Personalization Chamber
points_of_interest.description: Accessible by looking at ceilings throughout the castle (with 10+ stars). Contains a painting that leads to either Core Maze, Core Maze (beta), or Flesh Mountain depending on which portion is entered. The chamber 'personalizes' the path to the Core—different visitors get different routes. The castle CUSTOMIZES the journey to its heart based on the traveler.

subsections.name: Behind the Stained Glass — Peach's Route
subsections.description:
After defeating Bowser in the Castle, the visitor spawns behind the Princess Peach stained glass window and encounters Peach's APPARITION. She calls Mario's name. She leads the visitor down a hallway with an inaccessible balcony. She vanishes when approached, then reappears in a vertical shaft extending upward. Wall-jumping up the shaft brings the visitor to a tunnel ending at the back of the stained glass window, which exits to Vanilla Castle Grounds.

Waluigi has analyzed this sequence extensively. Peach's ghost is not a random haunting. She follows a SPECIFIC ROUTE. She appears, guides, disappears, reappears higher up, and ultimately leads the visitor to the back of her own memorial—where they can see the castle grounds from behind the glass that bears her image.

Peach's ghost wants visitors to see the world FROM HER PERSPECTIVE. She wants them to look out through her eyes—through the stained glass that commemorates her—and see the castle grounds as she sees them. A dead princess showing the living what the world looks like from the other side of a memorial.

If any of this intelligence reaches Captain Toadette and the Peach Loyalists, they will attempt to access this area. They will interpret Peach's ghost-guided tour as a DIVINE MANDATE. They will see a murdered princess reaching from beyond death to communicate with the living, and they will use it to justify ANYTHING.

Waluigi recommends this information be classified. Not because it's false—but because the truth, in the wrong hands, is more dangerous than any lie.

WAH.

sections.name: The Narrative Thread
sections.subtitle: Stories Written in Architecture
sections.overview: Waluigi has identified several narrative threads woven through the castle's connected spaces—stories told not through text but through the SEQUENCE of areas, the CONNECTIONS between them, and the CONSEQUENCES of traveling through them. These are not random collections of spaces. They are STORIES that the castle tells to anyone who follows the correct path.

subsections.name: The Bob-omb War Chronicle
subsections.description:
Follow the thread: Bob-omb Battlefield (beta) → River Mountain → Dark Downtown → Ice-Cold Warzone → Bob-omb's Revenge / Limitless Lighthouse.

The castle preserves the ENTIRE HISTORY of the Bob-omb conflict as a sequence of connected spaces. River Mountain represents the pre-war landscape—a peaceful area with a river, as the original designer intended. Bob-omb Battlefield (beta) is the war itself. Dark Downtown shows the civilian cost—a flooded town gone mad. Ice-Cold Warzone is the escalation—freezing conditions, rapid-fire cannons, Bob-ombs marching in place rather than patrolling, as if they've forgotten WHY they're fighting.

At the summit of Ice-Cold Warzone, the traveler faces a CHOICE: collect the Power Star (cosmic energy extraction) or enter the warp pipe. The star leads to Bob-omb's Revenge—a desolate battlefield where Prince Bob-omb waits with a timer counting up. Time is RUNNING OUT. The pipe leads to Limitless Lighthouse—a flooded, dead version of the battlefield where a dead Chain Chomp floats on the surface and mysterious remains litter the ocean floor.

The castle is asking: what do you choose? The star (power, but at the cost of revenge) or the lighthouse (knowledge, but surrounded by death)? Collecting the Limitless Lighthouse star loops back to Bob-omb Battlefield (beta)—the beginning. The war is a CYCLE.

Bob-omb Village extends this narrative. A pleasant community accessible from Bowser's Floor—but collecting a certain Power Star drains the village's energy, creating Dead Village. An icy wasteland where one house remains and its occupant is MISSING. The traveler's pursuit of cosmic energy DESTROYED a community. The sole survivor of a village entering the only remaining house leads to Beta Basement—death.

Prince Bob-omb appears in three locations: his stronghold Inside the Summit (where he can be defeated as a boss), Bob-omb's Revenge (where he waits with a timer), and Bob-omb Void (where his mangled body lies in an empty dimension, arms rearranged). The prince's story ends in mutilation displayed in nothingness. Even royalty cannot escape the castle's entropy.

subsections.name: The Peach Thread
subsections.description:
Princess Peach's presence permeates the castle despite—or because of—her death. Her stained glass windows hide passages. Her portraits conceal warps. Her ghost leads guided tours. Her voice echoes through corrupted floors. Her face appears on faceless paintings that kill those who enter them.

The sequence: Behind the Stained Glass (ghost-guided tour after defeating Bowser) → Vanilla Castle Grounds → Peach's Floor (pre-Bowser version) → Peach's Cell (dark hallway with Bowser paintings, Peach calling Mario's name, prison cell with open door) → Ruins in the Blood Lake.

Peach's Cell is particularly disturbing. Peach stands inside a cell whose door is OPEN. She is not imprisoned—she is CHOOSING to stay. Or she is unable to leave despite the lack of physical restraint. Touching the carpet in front of her cell warps to a black void with spotlights illuminating circles of checkerboard floor. A Power Star waits under the last spotlight. Collecting it leads to Ruins in the Blood Lake.

The castle tells Peach's story as a progression: memorial (stained glass) → haunting (ghost tour) → reign (her floor) → imprisonment (her cell) → destruction (blood lake). The open cell door is the cruelest detail—freedom exists but cannot be seized. This mirrors what Waluigi knows about Peach's assassination: she was not imprisoned by an enemy. She was betrayed by her own court. The cage was always open. The trap was the people around her.

points_of_interest.name: Peach's Floor vs. Bowser's Floor
points_of_interest.description: Two versions of the same space: Peach's Floor is the past (skylight, Toad statue, portrait, Boo-haunted hallway with warp to Peach's Cell or rarely Eternal Fort). Bowser's Floor is the future (bronze Toad statue, walled doorway, Bowser paintings, warp to Bob-omb Village). Standing on Bowser's throne in Bowser's Prison warps to Peach's Floor—Bowser's seat of power is a TIME MACHINE to Peach's era. Bowser sits on his throne and looks backward at what he conquered.

points_of_interest.name: The Faceless Peach Paintings
points_of_interest.description: Challenge Lobby contains a faceless Peach painting that warps to Challenge Library—where ENTERING the same faceless painting KILLS you and sends you to Beta Basement. The same image. One version transports safely. The other kills. In Challenge Lobby (corrupted), the faceless painting is MISSING entirely. The corruption consumed even the faceless memorial. Peach's identity has been erased in progressively more thorough stages: face removed, then the entire image.

subsections.name: The Judgment Sequence
subsections.description:
Tower Pinnacle → Judgment → Above the Clouds / Vanilla Lobby.

Judgment is a dimly-lit spiral staircase descending to a deep, black hole. Entering the hole with 33+ Power Stars leads to Above the Clouds—the castle's roof at nighttime, with a rainbow bridge to a higher tower containing Dream Castle. Entering with fewer than 33 stars returns you to Vanilla Lobby—the beginning.

The castle EVALUATES you. 33 is the threshold—the master number, the architectural signature. Below 33, you are returned to start. Above 33, you ascend. The castle's vertical axis (catacombs → basement → ground → upper floors → roof → clouds) is a spiritual hierarchy. The Judgment staircase is the GATEKEEPER between the castle's mortal levels and its celestial ones.
