summary: Mount Ebot is a 1,340-foot mountain in the Northern Reach with one T in its name, and that missing letter is the single most dangerous thing about it. The Old World Mapping Company's Survey Series IV chart prints it as MOUNT EBOT, one consonant away from Mount Ebott — the monster mountain four hundred miles east — and parties hunting the famous mountain have been arriving at the wrong one for as long as the plate has been in circulation. What they find is a cave that eats aircraft, a scree slope patrolled by a small silent figure that throws sharpened bones, ground that opens in parallel seams and hands back its dead, a maintained stone bridge fitted with sixty razors and six oil jets, and a burned plank naming four missing humans.
description:
# MOUNT EBOT
### Audit of a Mountain That Exists Because of a Typographical Error
### Filed by Waluigi, Auditor-General, Walupedia Editorial Board

Waluigi wishes to begin with the only sentence that matters, because everything else on this page is a consequence of it.

**Mount Ebot has one T. Mount Ebott has two. They are four hundred miles apart and they are not the same mountain, and there is a printing plate in circulation that does not know this.**

---

## 1. The Error Itself

The Old World Mapping Company's **Survey Series IV** chart of the Northern Reach carries, bottom right, a neat oval cartouche with a compass rose in it and the legend **CORRECTIONS ON APPLICATION**. Slightly north of centre it prints **MOUNT EBOT**.

Somewhere in the Company's composing room a clerk with cold hands set the type for *Ebott* and dropped a T, and the plate went to press, and the press went to market, and the market has been selling that plate ever since to expeditions who read the famous name, buy the chart, and fly north instead of east.

Waluigi has filed for the correction. The Company has not replied. Waluigi is not confident the Company still exists in any form capable of receiving a letter, which raises the interesting question of who is still printing from the plate.

> **The practical test — count the consonants before you charter an aircraft.** Mount **Ebott**: barrier, monsters, a king with a beard, an Iron Legion survey file. Mount **Ebot**: bones, razors, no treasure, and a bill.

---

## 2. The Approach and the Cave

The eastern face carries a near-permanent storm cell — rain in sheets, hail above two thousand feet, and a horizon that simply stops being a line. Roughly thirty feet up the face there is a black slot in the streaming rock, wide enough for a small aircraft and no wider, opening into a stone gallery some sixty feet deep with a floor of wet grit.

The gallery is survivable. It is not welcoming. Anything that comes in through the slot at speed will slide the length of the floor and lose its tail to the boulder at the back; anything that walks in will find the slope of scree below the slot moves when looked at.

---

## 3. The Sentry

A figure of roughly four feet holds the upper scree. Hooded or helmed — no observer has resolved which — with nothing under the brim that lightens when the sky does, and no breath in cold air.

It throws bones. Sharpened human femurs, dry and old, taken from the mountain rather than carried onto it, delivered with no windup at all. When pressed it does not flee: it stops occupying its position, with a soft fold of air and a smell like a struck match, and resumes throwing from eleven feet away on flat footing.

**It has never been heard to make a sound.** It withdraws entirely when the level ground is denied to it, and it does not pursue down the slope.

---

## 4. The Seams

The middle slope answers earthquakes by opening in three parallel seams, a foot wide, evenly spaced, running downhill — and pushing bones up through them along their whole length at once, the way a splinter is pushed out of a healing hand.

Within six hours the seams close, the mud goes smooth, and every bone is gone from the surface. Waluigi counted forty-one in a strip the size of a market stall on the ascent and found nothing at all on the descent, including a jaw with three teeth in it that he had specifically gone back to look for.

---

## 5. The Bridge

Ninety feet of mortared cut stone across a gorge, with a low parapet and proper drainage channels — an imperial-grade span built by people who expected to still be there in a century. Somebody improved it afterwards, and somebody is still servicing the improvements.

**Sixty razors** sit in machined slots along both parapets at knee and shin height, angled to catch a leg going forward. **Six brass nozzles** run beneath the deck, thumb-diameter, throats black with soot and smelling of lamp oil even in rain. **Six pale pressure plates** are set a fraction low in the stonework, graded by weight. After the span fires it **resets itself** with a series of small precise clicks and lies there looking like a bridge.

The threshold is heavy. A man of ordinary build can stand on a plate with his whole weight and the bridge will decline to consider him. Wario triggered every element of it and came off the far abutment on fire in three places, which established both the grading and the safe footprints.

---

## 6. The Plank

Past the bridge, where the path bends around a shoulder of rock, a hand-thick plank is bolted to two driven iron stakes. The lettering is burned in with a hot iron by a hand that got tired.

> **RIP — 4 MISSING HUMANS.** JAVIER. MIKAELA. DANIEL. And a fourth, burned in like the others and then greyed almost out of the wood: **PRINCE ALPHONSE.**

Three names are clean. The fourth has been worked over patiently with something soft and greasy until the burned grooves filled with grey, and can only be read at an angle against the light. Nobody burns a name into wood at that cost and removes it for tidiness.

The marker itself is ordinary practice — the Mushroom Treaty requires a party entering unmapped ground to leave the names of anyone it loses — which means somebody obeyed the paperwork on a hillside in the rain and then had second thoughts about exactly one entry.

---

## 7. The Staircase and the Summit

The last thousand feet are cut steps, two hundred and some of them, at least ninety worn into shallow dishes by centuries of traffic on a mountain that is supposed to be empty. Near the top, a squared niche the size of a lamp or an offering bowl is cut into the rock beside the stair, its rim carrying worn lettering in an unread alphabet and one **mason's survey index mark** of the type found on treaty-era boundary stones.

Someone official surveyed this mountain. Someone official cut a mark into it. And the chart that survey produced spells it with one T.

The summit is a cairn, a view of grey rain in every direction, and a second burned plank:

> **MOUNT EBOT — SUMMIT — 1,340 FT — NO FURTHER SERVICE**

There is no treasure. There has never been a claim of treasure attached to Mount Ebot by anybody. The claim belongs to the other mountain, and it arrives here by post. WAH.
notableFeatures: One T — the Old World Mapping Company Survey Series IV misprint that sends Mount Ebott expeditions four hundred miles the wrong way
The Slot — a black cave mouth thirty feet up the eastern face, wide enough for a small aircraft and no wider
The Silent Sentry — a four-foot hooded figure that throws sharpened femurs, folds the air to relocate, and has never made a sound
The Seams — parallel downhill fissures that push bones to the surface in rows during tremors and reabsorb them within six hours
The Improved Bridge — sixty parapet razors, six oil jets, six weight-graded pressure plates, and a self-reset; still being maintained
The Plank of Four — Javier, Mikaela, Daniel, and a Prince Alphonse whose name has been deliberately rubbed nearly out
The Dished Staircase — two hundred-plus cut steps worn hollow, with a survey-marked niche near the summit
NO FURTHER SERVICE — the summit plank, 1,340 feet, and no treasure of any kind

# IRON LEGION OLD WORLD EMBASSY
### Intake Site for the Mount Ebott Final Log

The embassy is the place where the Mount Ebott survey stopped being an expedition and became evidence. A helicopter lifted the Gamma Agent and Dracule Mihawk from the surface and delivered them to a roof where the corridors were white, the cameras were obvious, and the people pretending not to stare all knew the survey machine mattered.

The building's public face is diplomatic. Its working face is intake: collect the machine, separate witnesses, process the data, reward the asset, and decide what to do with a non-Legion swordsman who has seen too much. Waluigi files this as a location where architecture has learned to ask questions. The elevators do not merely move bodies between floors. They sort witnesses into procedures. WAH.

description:
# GAMMA HIGH COMMAND SPIRE
### The Place the Logger Went Dark

The High Command Spire is filed here because the final Mount Ebott log reaches it and then stops. The pilot says the flight will cross borders. The landscape disagrees. The helicopter lands before the passenger has finished objecting to the geography.

Inside, no guard challenges the Gamma insignia. An elevator climbs faster than a building has any right to permit. The chamber at the top contains three hooded figures, a request to disable the logger, and the last recorded sentence before the archive loses the room. Waluigi does not like buildings that make distance optional. Waluigi likes them even less when they also make records optional. WAH.

The Junction is mobility wearing brick. Whoever holds the mouths of the pipes can put a squad anywhere the old plumbers once bothered to connect. The map already had it as an unaligned ley-line POI. description:
The mansion is a dangerous, apparently abandoned property of long corridors, creaking floors, broken doors, neglected rooms, and a courtyard surrounded by dead trees. Its geometry is unreliable: a flight toward freedom returns to the grounds, while doors close in sequence when Alice chooses to pursue visitors.

A second-floor diary connected to Alice is believed to contain her memories and the means by which she holds Mario. The building is also the site of an unauthorized sample-retrieval mission, a failed DGK contact, Director Vale's arrival, and the emergence of a doppelgänger wearing Liam's face.

The site should not be treated as secure merely because a visitor reaches the courtyard. No signal, radio, or ordinary route has yet proved reliable.

description: **Forgotten Coastal Cove: A Tale of Trade and Ruin** Nestled along the verdant shores of the Great Bay, Forgotten Coastal Cove was once a bustling port city that thrived on its strategic position and rich natural resources. The cove offered easy access to the inland forests and mountains, as well as the vast open waters beyond. It was a place where traders from far and wide would come seeking wealth, and merchants would sell their wares in exchange for goods they could not produce at home. The name "Forgotten Coastal Cove" is fitting; today, it lies in a state of quiet abandonment, its once vibrant trade now reduced to ghostly echoes of its past. The docks are overgrown with vines and other lush plants that have taken root in the cracks and crevices of old stone. The port city's walls, which were once a symbol of prosperity and strength, now stand as silent witnesses to a bygone era. **The Golden Age** In the early days of Forgotten Coastal Cove, it was known for its bustling trade market. Merchants from nearby towns would come to trade their goods in exchange for salted meats, fish, fruits, and vegetables that were brought in through the port. The cove's location made it a crucial point in connecting these inland resources with the rest of the world. The harbor itself was a marvel of engineering during its heyday. Wide channels cut through the rocks to allow larger ships passage into the cove. These channels were lined with wooden piers, each one sturdy and well-built to support the weight of large cargo vessels. The piers had been built over centuries by the hardworking hands of local carpenters, and they were still in excellent condition when the cove was at its peak. The city itself was a marvel of architecture. Tall stone buildings lined the main street that ran parallel to the waterfront. Shops, taverns, and homes were all well-kept and vibrant with activity. The town square was a central gathering place where markets were held, and where local artisans could sell their goods. There were also several inns and hostels catering to the needs of travelers and merchants. **The Decline** However, the decline of Forgotten Coastal Cove began when the Great Bay's waters started to rise. This rise was attributed by some to a combination of natural forces and the wrath of Poseidon himself, who had been angered by the city’s lack of respect for his domain. The once-fertile land around the cove became increasingly swampy, and many of the surrounding towns faced similar problems. The port's channels began to silt up, making it difficult for larger ships to navigate into the harbor. This meant that smaller boats could still enter, but the large ships that had brought in much of the city’s wealth were no longer able to do so as efficiently or profitably. The loss of these vessels was a blow to the local economy and trade. As the port became less accessible, fewer merchants chose to travel there. With fewer visitors came a decline in business for many of the shops and taverns along the waterfront. The city’s population began to dwindle, and as more people left, so too did the resources that would have been needed to maintain the cove's infrastructure. **The Legend** There are those who believe Forgotten Coastal Cove is cursed. Legends speak of a powerful sorcerer who had once lived there. It was said he used his magic to ensure the city’s success and prosperity, but when his power waned or his heart turned sour, he placed an ancient curse on the town. This curse caused it to be abandoned by its people and left to nature's mercy. Others believe that the cove is simply a victim of time and neglect. The natural forces that brought about the rise in water levels were not entirely understood at the time, and the city could not adapt quickly enough to these changes. As the environment changed around it, so too did the livelihoods of its people. **The Present** Today, Forgotten Coastal Cove is a shadow of its former self. The once-proud stone walls that lined the main street are now crumbling. The piers have been overtaken by overgrowth and are in a state of disrepair. Some sections are still sturdy enough to support the weight of small boats, but many areas are too weak to be used safely. The town square is now covered with thick underbrush, which has grown up through cracks in the stone paving stones. The shops that once stood there are empty shells. In some cases, they have been converted into nests for birds and other wildlife who have found refuge in this abandoned place. The taverns that lined the main street no longer serve customers, but rather provide shelter for travelers seeking rest. The natural beauty of Forgotten Coastal Cove remains despite its neglect. Trees that once stood tall along the waterfront now bend and twist under the weight of time and storms. Their roots have taken hold in the cracks between stones and have helped to further erode the walls. The forest that surrounds the cove has reclaimed much of what was once open space, making it a haven for wildlife. Despite its current state, Forgotten Coastal Cove remains a place of interest for historians and curious visitors who want to see this once-thriving port city in all its ruinous glory. While many may come seeking adventure or mystery, they are also reminded of the fragility of human endeavor in the face of natural forces. The cove stands as both a monument to past prosperity and a cautionary tale about the importance of respecting nature's balance. **The Future** As the cove continues its slow transformation into a wilder state, there is hope that it will one day be rediscovered by those who recognize its value. Some local historians dream of restoring parts of the city to their former glory, creating a museum or park where visitors can learn about the cove’s rich history. Others envision a more practical use for the area, such as turning some of the buildings into artists' workshops or eco-friendly housing. No matter what the future holds, Forgotten Coastal Cove will continue to serve as a reminder that even places thought to be forgotten are never truly lost to time.

These statues are made from the same Fairystone as the walls but have suffered greatly over time due to weathering and neglect. Some still stand proudly, while others lie in pieces, scattered about the grounds. The statue of Toadstool the Brave is particularly notable; it once stood tall and proud, a reminder of the kingdom’s strong sense of justice and valor. The Mushroom Capitol was not only a center of governance but also a hub for cultural and technological development. Ancient libraries housed vast collections of scrolls and books that detailed the history, laws, and sciences of the Mushroom Kingdom. Unfortunately, these treasures have been lost to time, leaving behind only fragments and stories. Despite this loss, certain artifacts like ornate inkwells made from obsidian and gold have survived, testifying to the advanced craftsmanship of the kingdom’s artisans. The gardens that surrounded the palace are another testament to the once-thriving state of the Mushroom Capitol. The tools used by these artisans have long since been lost or stolen, but the layout of the workshops and the materials scattered around provide clues into the advanced nature of the kingdom’s industry. Despite its current state of ruin, the Mushroom Capitol retains a sense of reverence for those who visit. It serves as a reminder of the importance of preserving one's heritage and the fragility of grandeur in the face of time and change. The ruins are often visited by historians, archaeologists, and curious explorers who come to uncover secrets hidden beneath layers of decay. The story of the Mushroom Capitol’s rise and fall is one that resonates with many within the Mushroom Kingdom. It began during a period when Princess Peach's reign was at its zenith. Her leadership was marked by peace, prosperity, and unity among her subjects. The kingdom flourished under her rule, and the Mushroom Capitol became a symbol of this prosperity. However, it did not remain immune to the inevitable passage of time. By the time the Mushroom Capitol finally fell into ruin, it was a symbol not just of the past but also a warning for future generations about the importance of unity and resilience in the face of adversity. The grandeur of the city’s architecture stood in stark contrast to the quiet desolation that now surrounds its crumbling structures. Yet, within these ruins lies an enduring legacy — one that continues to inspire those who visit and study them. For today's explorers and historians, the Ruins of the Mushroom Capitol offer more than just a glimpse into the kingdom's past; they provide invaluable lessons about resilience in the face of adversity. Despite its current state, this place remains a powerful reminder of what once was, a testament to human ingenuity and ambition that persists even after centuries have passed.

name: Vellanet Rise
type: Location / Minor Landed Holding / Knight's Grant
region: Regal Empire — Midlands periphery, upriver of the Mighdural foothill roads
controllingFaction: The Order of Jack (grant held by Commander Jack Melvus Miser under Regal Empire tenure)

status: Active — quiet, solvent, and militarily unremarkable by every measure except its commander's reputation
summary: The grant Jack Miser earned rather than inherited: a fortified manor, three villages, a mill, a quarry and the road tolls between them, on the Regal Empire's Midlands periphery. Eleven miles of it, give or take the moor. It is the seat of the Order of Jack, the home of Wanda Miser and three of her children, and — measured against the empires this archive normally files — extremely small. That smallness is the point of the page.
description:
## Scale, Stated Plainly

Waluipedia's atlas is full of thrones, capitals, planar reflections and fortress-cities. Vellanet Rise is none of those. It is **a minor grant**: a fortified manor on a shoulder of high ground, three tenant villages below it, a mill on the river, a quarry cut into the ridge, and the toll rights on the road that ties them together.

A rider crosses it in a morning. A bad winter closes it twice. Its chief strategic value is that the road exists at all, and that somebody competent is now standing on it.

The archive is being deliberate about this figure because the alternative is worse. Jack Miser is a **lord of about eleven miles**, and every draft that quietly upgrades him to a realm makes the rest of his file dishonest.

## The Manor and the Yard

The manor is fortified rather than grand: a curtain wall a good siege engineer would call optimistic, a hall, a chapel with a Knowledge-Domain shrine that was not there before Lunaria started visiting, and a muster yard that is the only part of the estate built to a proper standard.

The yard tells you what the money went on. Stone underfoot, drainage that works, a smithy that is never cold, and stabling for far more horses than the household owns — because the order's mounted strength is the part of the roll that is real.

## The Villages

Three, named on the tenure roll and unremarkable on it: grain, sheep, gravel, and the mill. They pay the toll share, they raise the levy when called, and they have not been raided since the year the order stood up, which is the entire local argument for Jack's existence and the reason no one there cares what his muster roll says on paper.

## Who Lives Here

Wanda Miser keeps a set of rooms in the manor and, according to every account, keeps them exactly as plainly as she kept the last house. July, Spring and Hark come and go — funded, housed, and pointedly not enlisted. Jack's own quarters are next to the muster yard rather than over the hall, which is either humility or logistics, and Waluigi has stopped trying to establish which.

There is no room set aside for Archie. There is also no room given away.

## The Chapel, and the Two Villages That Do Not Use It

The estate's faith arrangement is the most interesting thing about it, and it is interesting for an unflattering reason: it is an unresolved problem that nobody has yet been forced to resolve.

The manor chapel is a **Silver Flame** foundation. That is not a choice Jack made. The Regal Lion swears its knights in a Flamekeep rite, the Order of Jack inherited the Lion's chaplaincy wholesale, and so the chapel on the shoulder keeps the Litany of Purification, funds a candle allowance, and reads the list of forbidden entities on Venerias like every other garrison chapel in the Midlands. Its congregation is overwhelmingly the garrison. The Knowledge-Domain shrine in the side aisle — Lunaria's, and not on any foundation document — is the only part of the building anyone visits voluntarily.

The **upper two villages keep the Lunar Cycle**, and have since before the manor existed. They keep it quietly, in the ordinary Midlands way: nobody howls at the moon within sight of the road, and the hill families come down for the mill and the market and go back up again.

The Church of the Silver Flame's standing edict on this subject is not ambiguous. *Edict of Purification: Inquisitors have free reign in allied territories.* The Rise is allied territory. Two of its three villages hold to a Primal Forces faith, which the compatibility register scores at **25 out of 100 against the Celestial Order** — the low end, "Minor Friction," well-meaning outsiders, ten per cent on ritual components, nobody burns.

Twenty-five is a survivable number. It is survivable because no inquisitor has come up the road and made it a question. The tenure roll records the upper villages as tenants. It does not record what they believe, and that omission is the single most deliberate piece of paperwork on the estate.

## The Order's Unwritten Instruction

The Order of Jack's chaplains are Flamekeep-ordained and receive one standing instruction that appears in no order book, no oath, and no muster return: **do not raise the Edict against a tenant of the Rise.**

Waluigi has confirmed the instruction exists from three separate serving chaplains, none of whom would put it on paper, all of whom described it in almost identical words. It is obeyed. It is also, strictly, a commander instructing ordained clergy to disregard a standing edict of their own church, which is a thing the archive would like everyone to notice is *not currently a crime only because nobody has filed it as one*.

Jack's position, when asked, was that the villages have paid the toll and raised the levy for four years and nobody has been raided, and that he was not going to be the man who arrived on a hill and made a neighbour into a heretic. It is a good answer. It is also an answer that assumes the person asking is him.

## Waluigi's Assessment

An honest little holding that runs well, protects its tenants, and would not survive contact with anything this archive normally files as a threat. Its defence is not its wall. Its defence is that it is too small to be worth the march — a security policy which works exactly until the day it doesn't.

And the thing that will end it will not be an army. It will be one inquisitor with a writ, walking up a road that is legally open to him, into two villages the tenure roll has been carefully vague about for four years. WAH.

Markop recognised it on arrival and walked to the stump they had stacked the loot on. You reach it by rope, through the tree's jaws, down a pit that a thrown torch does not measure. description:
Markop recognised it before anyone else did, and what he recognised is the whole entry: this is the Silent Grove. The party cleared it. They are standing in it again, inside something that was growing in a field an hour ago.

**The Approach**
There is no door. There is a mouth. When Markop pried the jaws of the trunk open he saw darkness first and a giant pit second, in that order, which is the order things arrive in here. The party threw a torch in as a test. The torch came back out of the trunk — and on the inside, Remi heard voices saying *there's a fire, someone's causing a fire, they're going to burn us all down*. That is the whole location in one exchange: you cannot sound it, and something in it is talking about you.

**The Heart**
At the centre stands a great, towering tree with vast branches reaching out to form a canopy over the area. Its boughs are coated in thick webs that are an unnerving mockery of foliage, and hanging from them are the forms of wrapped creatures, both beast and man, dangling like macabre fruit. The tree is long dead — some terrible malady killed it from the inside out years ago. Its dark roots jut from grey earth that no longer nourishes it, and its great arms serve as home to an unimaginable host of creeping, crawling arachnids that accost anything which wanders into their domain.

**What Lives Here**
Giant green spiders that fight with webs before they fight with fangs. Ettercaps that reel their targets in on a strand and open with a multiattack. And — filed with the discomfort it deserves — Legion soldiers, inside, alongside the brood, on ground no Legion column marched to.

**Fire**
Archie's fire bolt scarred the bark and did nothing else. Fire magic is weakened in this domain, which the wizard tested twice before believing it and then answered by emptying every reserve he had into a single cast. The tree took it. The exit did not survive.

**It Is the Silent Grove**
It is not a second one. Markop recognised it on arrival and named it: this is the Silent Grove, the web-choked forest on Raventree Manor's northwestern boundary where the party banished the Arachnid Matriarch. Same great dead tree, same web canopy, same grey earth. He walked to the broad flat stump at the roots — the stump the loot was stacked on that night, the War Mage's Staff he claimed on Archie's behalf, the Web-Woven Scale, the three healing potions — put a hand on it, and said so out loud. Nobody else in the party recognised it.

**Waluigi's Assessment**
So the archive is holding two facts that do not fit in the same box. The Silent Grove is on Raventree Manor's grounds and you reach it by walking. The Silent Grove is also inside the Scorncrow's tree and you reach it by rope, through a mouth, in the Shadowfell. Both are filed. Both are attested. Waluigi is not going to pretend that a place he helped clear has stayed cleared, or stayed put, and the open question is not whether this grove moved — it is whether it was ever only in one place. The Legion are standing in it. Somebody should ask how they walk there. WAH.

It is large, hot, heavily garrisoned, and exactly as welcoming as a volcano with a garrison. The Fawthful assault recorded on 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF proved the garrison was compromised from within: the dragon reached the castle, traitors opened paths for the attackers, and Bowser’s evacuation planning began before the walls were breached. In the current 1040 BF record Bowser is operating in the Shadow Estate; this castle damage is historical, not a present siege. Bowser is house-proud about it. Nobody else is.

Valley of Bowser maintenance tunnels

climate: Climate-controlled (emergency power configuration, 963 BF)

summary: E. Gadd's laboratory in the Guild District, connected by corridor networks to the Maglev Terminal Undercity. In 963 BF it was the staging room for the Clockwork Spire expedition; in the present day it is an abandoned lab with the paperwork to prove it used to matter.
description: Waluigi must begin with the laboratory because the laboratory is where the context lives. In 963 BF the Gadd Science Laboratory ran on emergency power while the expedition to the Clockwork Spire staged through its corridors, down through the network between the Guild District and the Maglev Terminal Undercity, and out onto the platforms. The present-day ruin keeps the same floor plan and none of the staff. Somewhere between the twelfth hour of Chillwind 8 and the modern era, the lights went out and nobody with a key came back.

name: Bowser's Mushroom Compound
region: Mushroom Kingdom (interior site, exact overworld position unfiled)
population: Garrisoned — Koopa troops; exact strength unfiled
climate: Volcanic; contained
status: Standing; entrance wall breached and lava-moat tunnel search filed after 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF
summary: The smaller of Bowser's known holdings: a walled volcanic annex inside the Mushroom Kingdom itself, run up through a warp-pipe riser to a lava bridge on the second floor, and drained below by a lava lake, a lava falls, and a calm moat at ground level. Waluigi ranks its hospitality below its parent castle's, which he did not think was physically possible. The later Garden Above the Fire search confirms the outflow and tunnel system did not just drain the compound; it hid Luigi long enough for the rescue to reach him.
description:
Waluigi had always assumed Bowser kept one address per kingdom out of vanity. The Mushroom Compound corrected him: a smaller fortification on Mushroom soil, close enough to the backroads that a man can drive to it in an evening and strange enough inside that the drive feels like the last normal thing that happened to him. The gate carries a security window and a guard with a button. The button opens the gate. Past it, a warp pipe rises to the second floor, where a stone bridge crosses open lava to a far ledge that holds exactly one furnishing: an axe in the stone, waiting for someone with a grievance and no plan. Below, the lava lake runs to a falls and spills out past the walls into a calm shore moat at ground level — the compound drains its own disasters outward, which is more than can be said for its owner. Neo Bowser City, by the guard's own account, is elsewhere, larger, and meaner; this place is the annex, and on the night of 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF, its entrance wall was burst open from the inside by a smiling man in blue overalls.

## The Lava-Moat Search

The lava bridge file left the compound owing the archive a search of the outflow. The Garden Above the Fire pays that debt: Wario's crew returned to the moat, took Kat and Ana's high-rock sighting seriously, and found Luigi alive in the volcanic tunnels beyond the falls. That search changes the compound from ambush site to rescue site too — the same drainage that nearly erased the truth preserved just enough of it to be found.

Warp-pipe riser to the second floor
The lava bridge and its bridge axe
Lava lake and lava falls below
Calm-shore moat at ground level, outside the walls
Entrance wall breach (18 Harvestide, 1035 BF)
Volcanic tunnel refuge where Luigi was found alive after the lava-falls drop

name: Dr. Toad's Star Hill Clinic
controllingFaction: Independent medical practice under Mushroom Kingdom civil protection
population: Small staff, anxious patients, and at least one doctor who insists Dr. Toad is his real name
climate: Cool hill air outside; lamplight, clean dressings, and antiseptic inside
status: Unreached — reported locked down with a 'private wing' as of 2 Aethel, 1035 BF; the street outside grew a mouth, the storehouse beside it took a helicopter on its roof, and a courier called the whole hill a 'rot-zone'
summary: A small Star Hill clinic where Wario's crew carried Luigi after recovering him from Bowser's lava outflow. Dr. Toad diagnosed serious but treatable burns, possible trauma delirium, and a strict ban on adventuring that Luigi immediately looked offended by.
description:
Dr. Toad's clinic sits close enough to the Star Hill roads that a group can reach it from the volcanic passages while still smelling of sulfur. The place is not a hospital palace; it is a practical night clinic — white sheets, glass bottles, clean bandages, a front desk that can panic at the sight of Wario carrying a limp plumber, and a physician cheerful enough to survive Waluigi asking if his name is actually Dr. Toad. On the night of 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF, it became the first quiet room after Bowser's compound: Luigi on the table, Wario blocking the doorway, Mona explaining too fast, Ashley hovering through an open window, and Waluigi pretending not to stand guard.

**2 Aethel, 1035 BF — the night the hill got a new name.** Two weeks after Luigi was carried in, a helicopter came for him and never reached the door. It caught its skid on the parapet of the storehouse next door, laid its rotor across the chimney and came to rest on its side on the roof, where a cracked fuel line burned on the stone and lit the clinic red. In the main street below, a man in Luigi's clothes recited verse at a courier; the courier shot him; the man lengthened, the cobbles split, and something with teeth and an eye on a stalk came up through the road and looked around. The courier went through the clinic's front window and came out of the storehouse stairwell. The storehouse itself would not keep its length — its stairwell grew while two men climbed it — and three copies of the man in green watched them leave by the fire ladder. The clinic's private wing, its patient, and its doctor were never seen. The courier's word for the hill was 'rot-zone', said like a word he had been issued.
notableFeatures: Front desk with a regrettably loud triage Toad
Emergency table where Luigi was treated for second-degree burns
Clean dressings and Mushroom Kingdom burn salves
Window used by Ashley rather than the door, because of course
The first room after the rescue where nobody was standing over lava
The flat storehouse roof next door, with a helicopter on its side against the chimney and a termination notice still clipped to the panel
The mouth in the main street — a seam of pink under a lid of broken cobbles, with an eye that looked around, in front of the clinic door
The front window, broken from the outside by a courier arriving at speed, and never repaired on the record
The storehouse stairwell that was longer on the way down than on the way up

name: Trinity General School
controllingFaction: Trinity General School administration; advisory authority delegated to SCHALE
population: A full student body; the filed roll for Classroom 2-B runs to eleven named students and an advisor
climate: Interior, temperate, fluorescent
status: Active — mid-term, newly assigned advisor, Classroom 2-B
summary: Trinity General School is the Kivotos academy where the archive's newest campaign opens. Kivotos was already in the record as Remi Akamatsu's birthplace — Residential District Seven, 12th Harvestide 1026 BF — and as a calendar the archive already carries; Trinity is the first building in it the archive has actually been inside. The relevant room is Classroom 2-B, which on the day of filing received a new advisor and discovered, mid-roll-call, that its curriculum is attached to SCHALE.
description:
The archive has held Kivotos at arm's length for a long time. It appears in Remi Akamatsu's file as the place she was born and left, in the wallet data as the issuer of Kivotos Credits, and in `calendars.json` as a four-term academic year with a six-day week and no true rest day. What it has not had is an interior.

Classroom 2-B is that interior.

**The room**
Desks in rows, a window line along one side, a whiteboard at the front, and a back row that functions as a separate jurisdiction. There is a door that slides rather than swings. The fluorescent lights are positioned such that a student standing directly in front of them can throw a silhouette across the room, which at least one student has worked out and uses deliberately.

**What the room is for**
On the evidence of the filing: roll call, announcements, and the delivery of information the students were evidently not briefed on beforehand. The advisor's stated remit is discipline and scheduling. The actual remit, disclosed in the same session, is SCHALE — deployment rotations, sector assignments, and hazard response.

**The seating, which is politics**
The front row is contested and was claimed by force of arrival. The window seats are sociable. The far corner is occupied by a student whose desk is angled away from the room. The back row holds the two students who do not participate and watch everything. Nobody assigned any of this.

**Waluigi's note:** a school where the timetable is a deployment rotation is not a school, it is a staging area with homework. Waluigi has read the roll. Eleven names, one advisor, and not one of those children was told what they were enrolled in until somebody asked a question the advisor answered honestly. WAH.
notableFeatures: Classroom 2-B — sliding door, window row, contested front row, and a back row that behaves as a separate jurisdiction
The whiteboard, on which the advisor drew a sector map of Kivotos's eastern perimeter and wrote THE RESISTANCE in underlined block capitals
The advisor's clipboard — carried constantly, tapped twice as a tell, and the physical object the roll call was read from
Fluorescent light bank at the front, used by at least one student as backlighting for declarations
planeClue: Kivotos is reached by the same transit network Remi Akamatsu crossed to arrive in the campaign; no planar markers in the filing itself

name: Kivotos
controllingFaction: No single authority — an academy federation with SCHALE as the coordinating body; the Resistance contests it from inside
population: Unrecorded; large enough to be divided into numbered residential districts and lettered operational sectors
climate: Urban temperate
status: Active — eastern perimeter sectors 7 through 12 under SCHALE deployment review after reported Resistance supply movement
summary: Kivotos is the academy city Remi Akamatsu was born in and left, and it has been in the archive's data for far longer than it has been in its prose — a calendar, a currency, a birthplace on one character sheet. The roll-call filing at Trinity General School is the first time the archive has stood inside it. Governance runs through academies rather than a crown, coordination runs through SCHALE, and the city is divided into numbered residential districts and lettered operational sectors.
description:
Kivotos has been quietly load-bearing in this archive for a long time without ever being written up.

**What the archive already held**
`Reputation-Matrix2/data/calendars.json` carries `kivotos_academic`: four ninety-day terms, a six-day week whose days are named Study, Lecture, Club, Field, Exam and Rest, five exam void days called Founder's Break, and a leap day every four years called Kaiser Day. Remi Akamatsu's file gives a birthplace — Kivotos, Residential District Seven, 12th Harvestide 1026 BF — and a wallet that carries Kivotos Credits, Credsticks and Data Chits alongside Midland Ducats. A city with its own calendar, its own money and an emigrant in the party is not a background detail.

**How it is organised**
Academies, not provinces. Trinity, Millennium and Shanhaijing are named in the calendar's `localTo` field as the bodies the academic year is local to. Remi's file names Gehenna Academy as a school she enrolled in and departed without formal withdrawal. The city is divided residentially into numbered districts and operationally into sectors; sectors 7 through 12 run along the eastern perimeter and hold warehouses, supply routes and abandoned industrial buildings.

**SCHALE**
Strategic Counter Hazard Activation League Execution. On the advisor's account it is the body that coordinates Knight deployments, allocates resources, and runs evacuation and hazard response — the difference, as he put it, between knowing there is a threat and doing something about it. It operates on a need-to-know basis. Student classes are attached to it, and at least one class did not know that until it was said out loud.

**The Resistance**
Described by the advisor, in the plainest terms he could manage for a room of confused students, as the bad guys: an internal threat operating from inside Kivotos, moving weapons through the eastern sectors. The archive records that as the advisor's characterisation and not as a finding. It is a one-sentence description of an armed political faction delivered to fourteen-year-olds, and no student in the room had the information to challenge it.

**The Equestrian question**
A diplomatic liaison programme exists between Kivotos and Canterlot — cultural exchange, small groups, intended to be quiet. Students saw liaisons walking the school openly. The advisor's reaction to being told this was not surprise at the programme but irritation at the breach, which is its own disclosure.

**Waluigi's note:** Kivotos has been sitting in this archive's calendar file for months like a folded map nobody opened. It has a six-day week with one rest day and the other five are named after work. Waluigi is not going to pretend that is subtle. WAH.
notableFeatures: Sectors 7 through 12 — the eastern perimeter: warehouses, supply routes, and abandoned industrial buildings described as good hiding places
Numbered residential districts — Remi Akamatsu was born in Residential District Seven
The Kivotos academic calendar: four 90-day terms, a six-day week (Study, Lecture, Club, Field, Exam, Rest), Founder's Break, and Kaiser Day every fourth year
Kivotos Credits, Credsticks and Data Chits — the city's tender, already carried in Remi Akamatsu's field wallet
The Equestrian liaison programme — a Canterlot diplomatic exchange that was supposed to be conducted quietly and was not
planeClue: reached via the transit network in Remi Akamatsu's backstory rather than a planar crossing; filed Material pending a better clue

name: The Feyward Basement (Cornivours Estate, Lower Level)
controllingFaction: Nominally Lady Aurelian and the Fey Court; functionally the Revel's kitchen staff and whatever the Orange Heir is organising
population: A satyr cellarer, a green hag, at least one goblin handler, and a stack of cages containing Goombas
climate: Warm candlelight, clear dripping water, the muffled noise of the party overhead
status: Structurally intact — the one part of the manor the overgrowth has not taken
summary: The level below the Overgrown Manor, and the Oracle's chosen drop point for Bowser because almost nobody lives down here and the building above is still standing. It holds a teleport circle on a sigil-marked floor, a drinks operation that supplies the Revel, a knight's statue, a corridor mouth with body parts in it, and a room of caged Goombas awaiting shipment.
description:
The Oracle picked this room for a reason and said the reason out loud: not much people reside down there and the building should still be in tact. Both halves of that sentence are true, and both are the point. The basement is the only part of the Overgrown Manor that is not being actively eaten.

Bowser arrived standing on a teleport circle set into a sigil carved in the floor. Beside it: a table, a bowl of blood, and candles that light the room warmly rather than ominously, which is somehow worse. A lever sits on the wall in what Bowser described as a state of begging to be touched. He did not touch it. The archive notes this as the single most restrained act of his career.

The blood in the bowl is not abandoned ritual scenery. It belongs to Mystic Morel — Purple T — who was using the room, came back for it, and was mildly put out to find a Koopa king standing in his workspace. He did not say what it was for.

Beyond the circle the level runs: a shield bearing the crest of Raventree, bones and candles underfoot, a locked door whose knob came off in Bowser's hand, cold storage stacked with labelled honey, a hallway containing a mouth with body parts inside it that Bowser edged around while calling it gross, a stairwell with ARULEAN'S FIRST KNIGHT engraved in stone beneath a statue holding a rusted sword, a cellar where a satyr plays cards against himself and keeps the drinks going up to the Revel, and a room of cages.

The cages are the part that matters. They hold Goombas — nine, by the handler's count — and they are inventory. A goblin directs their movement and a guard treats delivery as a chore to be handed to whoever is strong enough to carry it.
notableFeatures: Teleport circle on a carved floor sigil — the Oracle's delivery point, and the only confirmed route in
A table, a bowl of blood, and candles — an active workspace, not abandoned scenery; Mystic Morel claims the bowl
A lever on the wall that Bowser did not pull
A shield bearing the crest of Raventree — the estate names itself even in its Feywild mirror
Cold storage holding five labelled honeys: Warrior Honey, Honey of the Norn-Blessed, Honey of the Hearth Fire, Honey of the Hive Warden, Honey of the Sacred Bear
A corridor mouth with body parts inside it
A stairwell statue engraved ARULEAN'S FIRST KNIGHT, holding a rusted sword
The satyr's cellar — cards, drink production for the Revel above, and chained personal chests that resisted two punches
Cages of Goombas held as shipping inventory, handled by a goblin and guarded as routine freight
The building is intact; the overgrowth above has not reached this level
planeClue: Reached by the Oracle's teleport circle from the Planar Sanctum; the estate is named on site as the Cornivours estate and the crest is Raventree's.

name: Anamatar's Den
region: The Skittering Grove complex, off the burning grove
controllingFaction: Pierce Anamatar and his knights — inside Mages' Guild territory he does not recognise
population: A handful of knights, described by their master as more than a visitor can handle
climate: Dark, torchlit, roofed — the first room in the grove that is not made of web
status: Active — Remi, Wario and Mossy passed through it fleeing the spiders; a toll was charged
summary: The room the party stumbled into while running from the brood. It is Pierce Anamatar's holding, it is staffed with his knights, and it sits inside ground the Mages' Guild claims — a fact Anamatar raises himself, and volunteers that he does not like the Guild. Passage out is available. It is not free.
description:
Waluigi files this as a location rather than a scene because a room where somebody sets prices is a place of business.

Wario came in punching and found nothing to punch. The room was already occupied: wrights standing in the dark, and then Anamatar himself, arriving to ask why a stranger was fighting his people in his den.

What followed was a negotiation conducted between a man who was frightened and a man who enjoyed that. Wario said he was running from the spiders. Anamatar asked whether he was afraid of a few creepy-crawlies and offered him a bandaid and a sippy cup. Wario said yes, he was, and asked whether Anamatar had seen what they look like.

Then the terms. This is Guild-controlled ground; Anamatar does not like the Guild; he will send them back where they came from **in exchange for something of theirs**. He asked first for the siglet — the ring the party has been chasing since Tymnas's lodge — and settled for [Remi's](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) student ID card, on the grounds that it is very durable.

Waluigi notes the shape of the deal and not its size. The man did not want money. He wanted a **thing that belongs to somebody**, and he took the one piece of paper in the grove that proves a fourteen-year-old was ever enrolled anywhere.

name: The Nintendo Mania Studio
planeClue: Newspaper claims Hollywood / Los Angeles; no other filing corroborates the coordinate
region: Unrecorded — reached by falling out of the sky during the pilot's taping
climate: Climate-controlled on a schedule: warm break room, hot coffee, then fire, then sprinklers, then ice
population: Three visitors, one real Mario, one Luigi, one corrupted Mario, a paratroopa squad in studio uniforms, one unconscious Wario, one Director — and an applause track for an audience that is not there
controllingFaction: None filed — the studio answers to Director Mario, who answers to nobody on record
summary: The studio where the Nintendo Mania pilot is taped, and where two filings of the Mario disappearance file have now taken place. Its exits lie — doors reset, portals fail, emergency buttons make coffee — but its ceiling vents, its sprinklers, its paratroopa rescue squad, and its curtains are all real. It resets itself when told CUT.
description: The studio files itself as a building with a production schedule. The Nintendo Mania pilot set, the employee break room with its four monitors and its coffee machine, the kitchen back door, the ceiling ducts with their rats, the maintenance room with the working computer, the corridors where the corrupted Mario hunts, and the stage where the curtains come down. Two accounts agree on the geometry and disagree on nothing except whether any of it is load-bearing. The break room resets — the same couch, the same monitors, the same coffee machine, and after the CUT a single television showing static. The exits are traps: the back door leads to the kitchen, the front door led to the fake Luigi, the portal home printed FAILED. The escape route was a ceiling vent opened by a coffee machine's steam, and the building's own safety systems — sprinklers, a paratroopa squad, a fire alarm with real glass — behaved exactly as advertised while everything around them performed. The archive's standing question is not where the studio is. It is who the show is for, because the seats are empty and the applause plays anyway.
notableFeatures: The EMERGENCY EXIT button by the coffee machine — pressing it makes coffee
The ceiling vent that the coffee machine's steam pops open
Four break-room monitors; Camera Three once showed a black-eyed fake Luigi
The maintenance computer: security feeds, a studio map, notes on Wario's corruption
Theatrical curtains on the whole ceiling, deployed on someone's cue
A paratroopa rescue squad in studio uniforms with parachute rigs
An applause track that plays to an empty, silent facility
status: Active — the show was interrupted, not cancelled; the Director walked out with a remote

name: Waluigi's Outpost
region: The slope below Wario's mountaintop residence, Mushroom Kingdom interior
population: One archivist, several hundred filings, and whatever the wind brings up the slope
climate: Cold stone and candle smoke; night air off the mountain carries woodsmoke from the city below
summary: The stone house where Waluigi lives and drafts. A balcony with a patio table faces the night sky and, unavoidably, Wario's residence on the peak above — a sightline that works in both directions. Inside, the main study: towering shelves, drafting tables of maps and scrolls, and the working papers of the 'No Longer Brothers' revision.
description: Waluigi files his own address under protest, because the Debt Siege made it canon: the balcony where Revision 2 was read aloud, the heavy oak study door that stopped a W-stamped mechanical fist for exactly four strikes, and the frost scars where an Ice Storm and a borrowed Flash-Freeze sealed a scholar's own life's work behind a wall of ice to save it. The study survived. The door is a write-off. The ledger of what is owed for the frame is, per the owner, a matter for Wario's conscience, an organ whose existence remains unverified.

The main study: towering shelves, drafting tables, maps and scrolls
The oak study door — splintered, frozen, and furious about both
Frost damage from the Flash-Freeze wall of 2 Aethel, 1035 BF

name: Fawful's Bean Badge
controllingFaction: Fawful (proprietor, 955 BF) — Mages' Guild operatives in the back room by the only account
status: Historical — trading in Efferd, 955 BF; no shop of the name trades in Toad Town in 1040 BF and the archive has not found the drain that reached it
summary: A bean shop in Toad Town with Fawful's name over the counter: jars of beans on the shelves, a tray of enamel badges by the till, and a cellar that connects to the warp drains under Peach's Castle closely enough that a lost ceremonial guard reached it from the dungeon in five hours with a letter for a map. On the one night the archive has it, the shop held the Koopa who was never locked in, two Mages' Guild operatives, a Goomba on a sack by the door, Fawful in a borrowed Guild cloak, and the plan for the vacuum shroom. Waluigi files it as a front, because a shop that a dead palace guard carried directions to in his coat is not selling beans.
description:
The Bean Badge is on the archive's map for one dawn. Everything below is from the account filed as [The Unlocked Cell](#/article/the_unlocked_cell_955_bf), which reached the shop through a grate and a cellar at about six in the morning in Efferd, 955 BF, and never left it on the record.

## The Shop

Small. Shelves of glass jars — beans, by the account, which did not inspect them — a counter, a tray of badges, lamps still lit against a grey window. A sign with Fawful's name on it, remembered by the account imperfectly. A Goomba sat by the door on a sack like a shop cat. The word *Badge* in the name is the shop's and not the archive's; what the badges were for, who wore them, and whether the tray on the counter was stock or a register are open.

## The Cellar and the Drain

John Lee came up into the shop from below — a grate, a cellar, the shop — after five hours in the warp system under Peach's Castle. The account does not map the route. It establishes that a route exists, that it runs from the palace dungeon to this cellar, and that it is navigable by a ceremonial guard with a lantern and no training, which means it was built to be navigated. The Koopa who left the dungeon ahead of him was already upstairs.

## Who Was In It

The Koopa prisoner, with the fat vial. Two Mages' Guild operatives — the people who told the father his son was being taken care of, and who asked him whether he was stupid for wanting an escort from people he had just said he did not trust. A Goomba. And Fawful, who put on a Mages' Guild cloak over the red to explain the vacuum shroom — inhaled, the Koopa King sucks up everything in reach, the brothers included; the castle's wards still active; *dispatch of this finkrat and takeover kingdom* — and whom the two operatives did not correct.

## Why It Is a Front

A dead palace guard in the hall of Peach's Castle had *meet me in Fawful's bean shop* in his livery before the shop had been mentioned to anyone. The Guild met there. The Koopa reported there. The plan was explained there. The archive has one bean shop in 955 BF that doubles as the Arrangement's back office and it is this one, and the archive would like to know what the Regency's first year did with it, because by 1040 BF nothing trades under the name and nobody in Toad Town remembers a bean shop with a cellar.
notableFeatures: A sign with Fawful's name — remembered by the account, not read
The badge tray on the counter: a shop card from it is filed as an exhibit
A cellar grate onto the warp drains that run to the palace dungeon — five hours, by lantern, with a letter for a map
The vacuum shroom and the fat vial, explained here and not yet used
A Goomba on a sack by the door
planeClue: Toad Town, under the castle's drains — the Material capital as it stood before Highsun 1, 955 BF

name: The Town Beneath the Legionlance (name not recorded)
region: Near the Ruined Manor, in sight of the Legionlance's mooring
population: Legion garrison, shopkeepers, a gate guard with a baton and a doctor with a saw
climate: Early morning; everyone is being told to smile
status: Garrisoned and braced for an execution — the party passed through on foot, bought and sold at the one shop, and was told where to find a prosthetist
summary: A small Legion-held town within sight of the Legionlance, which the party walked into from the ruined manor on 1 Aethel, 1040 BF. Its guards are strict about smiling, its shop will buy anything and offer a third of it, and its square was being readied for the execution of Kyle Coinsoul under Commander G. The town's own name never came up; Waluigi files it by what it sits under.
description:
The town has one shop that matters and one rumour that matters. The shop sells binoculars, packs, ink, candles and a magnifying glass at a hundred gold, and buys back at the prices of a shop that knows nobody else will. The rumour is a prosthetist named Rudy Lee, who is said to be very hands on and to prefer the patient awake.

The guard at the edge of town asked the party what they were doing out so early and told them to put on a smile while they stayed. The reason was the execution. The shop looks up the hill at the ship.
notableFeatures: The shop: binoculars, packs, ink, candles — and the buyer who offered 15 gold for a 50-gold bar
The order to smile while Kyle Coinsoul is brought out
Rudy Lee, the prosthetist the shop knows of
A clear line of sight to the Legionlance at its mooring
planeClue: Legion garrison under the Legionlance, reached on foot from the Material-side ruined manor
